title.zh: 卷二百三十八 列傳第一百二十六 李成梁 麻貴
title.en: Volume 238 Biographies 126: Li Chengliang, Ma Gui
title.raw: 卷二百三十八 列傳第一百二十六 李成梁 麻貴 Volume 238 Biographies 126: Li Chengliang, Ma Gui

sentences.zh: 李成梁子:如松 如柏 如楨 如樟 如梅 麻貴兄:錦

translations.literal: Li Chengliang's sons: Rusong, Rubai, Ruzhen, Ruzhang, Rumei; Ma Gui's elder brother: Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of Li Chengliang: Rusong, Rubai, Ruzhen, Ruzhang, and Rumei; elder brother of Ma Gui: Jin.

sentences.zh: 李成梁

translations.literal: Li Chengliang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengliang

sentences.zh: 李成梁，字汝契。

translations.literal: Li Chengliang, styled Ruke.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengliang, whose style name was Ruke.

sentences.zh: 高祖英自朝鮮內附，授世鐵嶺衛指揮僉事，遂家焉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Ying came from Korea to submit to the dynasty, was appointed hereditary assistant commander of the Tieling Guard, and the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Ying had come from Korea to enter Ming service and received appointment as hereditary assistant commander of the Tieling Guard; the family made its home there.

sentences.zh: 成梁英毅驍健，有大將才。

translations.literal: Chengliang was resolute, brave, and stalwart, with the talent of a great general.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang was bold, resolute, and physically formidable, and showed the makings of a great commander.

sentences.zh: 家貧，不能襲職，年四十猶為諸生。

translations.literal: His family was poor and he could not inherit the office; even at forty he remained a student.
translations.idiomatic: The family was too poor for him to inherit his father's post, and he was still only a licentiate at the age of forty.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史器之，資入京，乃得襲。

translations.literal: A touring censor recognized his ability, funded his journey to the capital, and only then could he inherit the post.
translations.idiomatic: A touring censor took notice of his ability, paid his way to the capital, and only then was he able to succeed to the office.

sentences.zh: 積功為遼東險山參將。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he became regional vice commander of Xianshan in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: By accumulated service he rose to regional vice commander at Xianshan in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年，士蠻大入永平。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing, Tümen invaded Yongping on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Longqing reign, Tümen launched a major raid into Yongping.

sentences.zh: 成梁赴援有功，進副總兵，仍守險山。

translations.literal: Chengliang went to the relief with merit, was promoted to vice commander-in-chief, and continued to guard Xianshan.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang marched to relieve the district with distinction, was promoted to vice commander-in-chief, and continued to hold Xianshan.

sentences.zh: 尋協守遼陽。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he jointly guarded Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon assigned to help defend Liaoyang as well.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，張擺失等屯塞下，成梁迎擊斬之，殲其卒百六十有奇。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, Zhang Baishi and others encamped below the pass; Chengliang met them in battle, beheaded them, and annihilated more than one hundred sixty of their soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year three, Zhang Baishi and his followers camped below the border pass; Chengliang met them in battle, killed them, and wiped out over one hundred sixty of their men.

sentences.zh: 餘眾遠徙，遂空其地。

translations.literal: The remaining forces migrated far away, and the land was thereby emptied.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors withdrew far away, leaving the region depopulated.

sentences.zh: 錄功，進秩一等。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and his rank was advanced one grade.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were entered in the record and his rank was raised one step.

sentences.zh: 四年九月，辛愛大入遼東。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year, Xin'ai invaded Liaodong on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year four, Xin'ai led a major incursion into Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 總兵官王治道戰死，擢成梁署都督僉事代之。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief Wang Zhidao died in battle; Chengliang was promoted to acting regional commander and replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-chief Wang Zhidao fell in battle, and Chengliang was elevated to acting regional commander to take his place.

sentences.zh: 當是時，俺答雖款塞，而插漢部長土蠻與從父黑石炭，弟委正、大委正，從弟暖兔、拱兔，子卜言台周，從子黃台吉勢方強。

translations.literal: At that time, although Altan Khan had pledged peace at the border, the Chahar chieftain Tümen, together with his father's younger brother Heishitan, his younger brothers Weizheng and Daweizheng, his younger cousins Nuantu and Gongtu, his son Buyan Taiju, and his nephew Huang Taiji, were growing powerful.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Altan Khan had made peace with the border, but the Chahar leader Tümen—along with his uncle Heishitan, his brothers Weizheng and Daweizheng, his cousins Nuantu and Gongtu, his son Buyan Taiju, and his nephew Huang Taiji—were all rising in strength.

sentences.zh: 泰甯部長速把亥、炒花，朵顏部長董狐狸、長昂佐之。

translations.literal: The Taining chieftains Subanhai and Chaohua, and the Tümed chieftains Donghuli and Chang'ang, assisted them.
translations.idiomatic: They were aided by the Taining leaders Subanhai and Chaohua and by the Tümed leaders Donghuli and Chang'ang.

sentences.zh: 東則王杲、王兀堂、清佳砮、楊吉砮之屬，亦時窺塞下。

translations.literal: In the east, Wang Gao, Wang Wutang, Qinggianu, Yanggianu, and their like also watched for chances below the passes.
translations.idiomatic: To the east, Wang Gao, Wang Wutang, Qinggianu, Yanggianu, and others likewise probed the border from time to time.

sentences.zh: 十年之間，殷尚質、楊照、王治道三大將皆戰死。

translations.literal: Within ten years the three great generals Yin Shangzhi, Yang Zhao, and Wang Zhidao all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Within a decade the three senior commanders Yin Shangzhi, Yang Zhao, and Wang Zhidao had all been killed in action.

sentences.zh: 成梁乃大修戎備，甄拔將校，收召四方健兒，給以厚餼，用為選鋒。

translations.literal: Chengliang thereupon greatly strengthened military preparations, selected and promoted officers, gathered stalwart men from all quarters, gave them generous rations, and used them as assault troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang then set about rebuilding the army in earnest: he picked out capable officers, recruited tough fighters from every direction, paid them well, and formed them into an elite strike force.

sentences.zh: 軍聲始振。

translations.literal: The army's reputation began to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the army's reputation begin to recover.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，敵犯盤山驛，指揮蘇成勳擊走之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the following year, the enemy attacked Panshan Post; Commander Su Chengxun drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the fifth month, the enemy struck Panshan Post and was beaten back by Commander Su Chengxun.

sentences.zh: 無何，土蠻大入。

translations.literal: Before long, Tümen invaded on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Tümen launched another major raid.

sentences.zh: 成梁遇于卓山，麾副將趙完等夾擊，斷其首尾。

translations.literal: Chengliang met him at Zhuoshan, ordered Vice Commander Zhao Wan and others to attack from both sides, and cut off his van and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang met him at Zhuoshan and sent Vice Commander Zhao Wan and others to strike from both flanks, severing the head and tail of his column.

sentences.zh: 乘勝抵巢，馘部長二人，斬首五百八十餘級。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory to their camp, he took the heads of two chieftains and more than five hundred eighty severed heads in all.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the victory to their camp, killed two tribal leaders, and took more than five hundred eighty heads.

sentences.zh: 進署都督同知，世廕千戶。

translations.literal: He was promoted to acting regional vice commander and granted hereditary enfeoffment as a chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to acting regional vice commander and granted hereditary rank as a chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 又明年十月，土蠻六百騎營舊遼陽北河，去邊二百餘里，俟眾集大舉，成梁擊走之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the year after that, Tümen encamped with six hundred horsemen on the north bank of the old Liao River, more than two hundred li from the border, waiting for his forces to gather for a major campaign; Chengliang attacked and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: The following October, Tümen camped with six hundred horsemen on the north bank of the old Liao River, over two hundred li beyond the border, to await reinforcements for a major strike; Chengliang routed him.

sentences.zh: 萬曆元年，又擊走之前屯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wanli he again drove them off at Qiantun.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Wanli reign he again repulsed them at Qiantun.

sentences.zh: 已，又破走之鐵嶺鎮西諸堡。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he again defeated and drove them off at the forts west of Tieling garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he broke and chased them away from the forts west of Tieling.

sentences.zh: 增秩二等。

translations.literal: His rank was raised two grades.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was raised two steps.

sentences.zh: 朵顏兀露絲罕以四千騎毀牆入，成梁禦卻之。

translations.literal: The Tümed leader Ulusihan entered with four thousand horsemen by breaking through the wall; Chengliang repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: The Tümed leader Ulusihan breached the wall with four thousand horsemen, but Chengliang drove him back.

sentences.zh: 建州都指揮王杲故與撫順通馬市。

translations.literal: Wang Gao, regional commander of Jianzhou, had formerly traded horses with Fushun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gao, regional commander of Jianzhou, had long conducted the horse market at Fushun.

sentences.zh: 及是，誘殺備禦裴承祖，成梁謀討之。

translations.literal: At this time he lured and killed Battalion Commander Pei Chengzu; Chengliang planned to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Now he lured and killed Battalion Commander Pei Chengzu, and Chengliang resolved to bring him to account.

sentences.zh: 明年十月，杲復大舉入。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the following year, Gao again invaded on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: The next October, Gao raided again in force.

sentences.zh: 成梁檄副將楊騰、遊擊王惟屏分屯要害，而令參將曹簠挑戰。

translations.literal: Chengliang ordered Vice Commander Yang Teng and Mobile Corps Commander Wang Weiping to garrison key points separately, and had Regional Vice Commander Cao Lin provoke battle.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang sent Vice Commander Yang Teng and Mobile Corps Commander Wang Weiping to hold the critical passes while Regional Vice Commander Cao Lin drew the enemy out to fight.

sentences.zh: 諸軍四面起，敵大奔，盡聚杲寨。

translations.literal: The armies rose on all four sides; the enemy fled in great disorder and all gathered in Gao's stockade.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming forces closed in from every side; the enemy broke and fled, crowding into Gao's fortress.

sentences.zh: 寨地高，杲深溝堅壘以自固。

translations.literal: The stockade stood on high ground; Gao dug deep ditches and built strong ramparts to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: The fortress stood on high ground, and Gao dug deep trenches and threw up strong walls to hold his position.

sentences.zh: 成梁用火器攻之，破數柵，矢石雨下。

translations.literal: Chengliang attacked with firearms, broke several palisades, and arrows and stones fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang assaulted it with firearms, smashed several palisades, and brought down a storm of arrows and stones.

sentences.zh: 把總于志文、秦得倚先登，諸將繼之。

translations.literal: Company commanders Yu Zhiwen and Qin Deyi were first to scale the walls; the other generals followed.
translations.idiomatic: Company commanders Yu Zhiwen and Qin Deyi led the assault over the walls, and the other officers pressed in after them.

sentences.zh: 杲走高臺，射殺志文。

translations.literal: Gao went up a high platform and shot Zhiwen dead.
translations.idiomatic: Gao climbed a high platform and shot Zhiwen dead.

sentences.zh: 會大風起，縱火焚之，先後斬馘千一百餘級，毀其營壘而還。

translations.literal: A great wind arose; they set fires and burned the place, taking in all more than eleven hundred severed heads before and after, destroyed the camps and ramparts, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: A strong wind sprang up; they set the fortress ablaze and in the end took more than eleven hundred heads, wrecked the camps, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 進左都督，世廕都指揮同知。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Regional Commander and granted hereditary enfeoffment as regional vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Regional Commander and granted hereditary rank as regional vice commander.

sentences.zh: 杲大創，不能軍，走匿阿哈納寨。

translations.literal: Gao was gravely wounded, could not keep his army together, and fled to hide in the Ahanazhai stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was badly wounded, could no longer hold his forces together, and fled to hide in the stockade at Ahanazhai.

sentences.zh: 曹簠勒精騎往，杲走南關。

translations.literal: Cao Lin led elite cavalry in pursuit; Gao fled to Nanguan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Lin rode after him with picked cavalry, and Gao fled toward Nanguan.

sentences.zh: 都督王台執以獻，斬之。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Wang Tai seized him and presented him; he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Wang Tai seized him and handed him over; Gao was then executed.

sentences.zh: 三年春，土蠻犯長勇堡，擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year, Tümen attacked Changyong Fort and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year three, Tümen struck Changyong Fort and was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 其冬，炒花大會黑石炭、黃台吉、卜言台周、以兒鄧、暖兔、拱兔、堵剌兒等二萬餘騎，從平虜堡南掠。

translations.literal: That winter, Chaohua assembled Heishitan, Huang Taiji, Buyan Taiju, Yierdeng, Nuantu, Gongtu, Dulai'er, and others—more than twenty thousand horsemen—and raided south from Pinglu Fort.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Chaohua mustered Heishitan, Huang Taiji, Buyan Taiju, Yierdeng, Nuantu, Gongtu, Dulai'er, and others—over twenty thousand horsemen—and swept south past Pinglu Fort.

sentences.zh: 副將曹簠馳擊，遂轉掠瀋陽。

translations.literal: Vice Commander Cao Lin rode in pursuit; they then turned to plunder Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commander Cao Lin gave chase, whereupon they swung toward Shenyang to loot.

sentences.zh: 見城外列營，乃據西北高墩。

translations.literal: Seeing camps arrayed outside the city, they seized the high mound in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Ming camps drawn up outside the walls, they occupied a high mound to the northwest.

sentences.zh: 成梁邀戰，發火器。

translations.literal: Chengliang offered battle and deployed firearms.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang met them in battle and opened fire with firearms.

sentences.zh: 敵大潰，棄輜重走。

translations.literal: The enemy collapsed in great disorder, abandoned their baggage, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy broke in rout, abandoning their baggage train as they fled.

sentences.zh: 追至河溝，乘勝渡河，擊斬以千計。

translations.literal: The pursuit reached Hegou; pressing the victory they crossed the river and killed and beheaded on the order of a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit carried to Hegou; riding their momentum they crossed the river and cut down the enemy by the thousand.

sentences.zh: 加太子太保，世廕錦衣千戶。

translations.literal: He was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted hereditary enfeoffment as a chiliarch of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted hereditary rank as a chiliarch in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 明年，黑石炭、大委正營大清堡邊外，謀錦、義。

translations.literal: The following year, Heishitan and Daweizheng encamped outside the border by Daqing Fort, plotting against Jinzhou and Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Heishitan and Daweizheng camped beyond the border near Daqing Fort, with designs on Jinzhou and Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 成梁率選鋒馳二百里，逼其營，攻破之。

translations.literal: Chengliang led his assault troops in a two-hundred-li dash, pressed their camp, and stormed it.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang led his strike force on a two-hundred-li ride, closed on their camp, and overran it.

sentences.zh: 殺部長四人，獲級六十有奇。

translations.literal: Four chieftains were killed and more than sixty severed heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Four tribal leaders were killed and more than sixty heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 五年五月，士蠻復入，聯營河東，而遣零騎西掠。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year, Tümen invaded again, linked camps east of the river, and sent scattered horsemen to raid westward.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year five, Tümen struck again, massing his camps east of the river while detachments harried the west.

sentences.zh: 成梁掩其巢，得利而還。

translations.literal: Chengliang surprised their base, gained the advantage, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang fell on their base by surprise, took his profit, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，速把亥糾土蠻大入，營劈山。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, Subanhai rallied Tümen for a major invasion and encamped at Pishan.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the first month, Subanhai joined Tümen in a major raid and pitched camp at Pishan.

sentences.zh: 成梁馳至丁字泊，敵方分騎繞牆入。

translations.literal: Chengliang galloped to Dingzipo; the enemy had already sent detachments of horsemen around the wall to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang raced to Dingzipo, but the enemy had already sent parties of horsemen around the wall to break in.

sentences.zh: 成梁夜出塞二百里，搗破劈山營，獲級四百三十，馘其長五人。

translations.literal: Chengliang went out of the pass by night for two hundred li, stormed the Pishan camp, took four hundred thirty severed heads, and five chieftains' heads.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang marched two hundred li beyond the border by night, smashed the camp at Pishan, took four hundred thirty heads, and killed five leaders.

sentences.zh: 加太保，世廕本衛指揮使。

translations.literal: He was made Grand Mentor and granted hereditary enfeoffment as commander of his original guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Mentor and granted hereditary rank as commander of his home guard.

sentences.zh: 三月，遊擊陶承嚳擊敵長定堡，獻馘四百七十有奇。

translations.literal: In the third month, Mobile Corps Commander Tao Chengyin attacked the enemy at Changding Fort and presented more than four hundred seventy severed heads.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Mobile Corps Commander Tao Chengyin fought the enemy at Changding Fort and reported more than four hundred seventy heads taken.

sentences.zh: 帝已告謝郊廟，大行賞賚，廕成梁世指揮僉事。

translations.literal: The emperor had already announced thanks at the suburban altars and bestowed rewards on a grand scale, enfeoffing Chengliang's heir as assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already offered thanks at the suburban altars and lavished rewards, enfeoffing Chengliang's heir as assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 有言所殺乃土蠻部曲，因盜牛羊事覺，懼罪來歸，承嚳掩殺之。

translations.literal: Some said those killed were Tümen's followers who, their theft of cattle and sheep having been discovered, had come to surrender in fear of punishment, and that Chengyin had slaughtered them in an ambush.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread that the dead were in fact Tümen's men who, caught stealing livestock, had surrendered in fear of punishment—and that Chengyin had cut them down in a treacherous attack.

sentences.zh: 給事中光懋因請治承嚳殺降罪，御史勘如懋言。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Guang Mao thereupon asked that Chengyin be punished for killing those who had surrendered; the censor's investigation confirmed Mao's account.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Guang Mao then called for Chengyin to be punished for slaughtering men who had surrendered, and the censor's inquiry upheld his charge.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書方逢時，督撫梁夢龍、周詠先與承嚳同敘功，力為解。

translations.literal: Minister of War Fang Fengshi and the grand coordinators Liang Menglong and Zhou Yong, who had earlier recorded merit together with Chengyin, strenuously pleaded on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Fang Fengshi and the grand coordinators Liang Menglong and Zhou Yong—who had shared in crediting Chengyin's victory—argued strenuously in his defense.

sentences.zh: 卒如御史奏，盡奪諸臣恩命。

translations.literal: In the end the censor's memorial was followed, and all the favors granted the officials were revoked.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the court followed the censor's report and stripped all the officials of their rewards.

sentences.zh: 六月，敵犯鎮靜堡，復擊退之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the enemy attacked Zhenjing Fort and was again driven back.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the enemy struck Zhenjing Fort and was repulsed once more.

sentences.zh: 十二月，速把亥、炒花、暖兔、拱兔會土蠻黃台吉，大、小委正，卜兒亥，慌忽太等三萬餘騎壁遼河，攻東昌堡，深入至耀州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Subanhai, Chaohua, Nuantu, and Gongtu joined Tümen, Huang Taiji, Daweizheng, Xiaoweizheng, Bu'erhai, Huanghutai, and others—more than thirty thousand horsemen—who lined the Liao River, attacked Dongchang Fort, and penetrated as far as Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Subanhai, Chaohua, Nuantu, and Gongtu joined Tümen, Huang Taiji, the Daweizheng and Xiaoweizheng brothers, Bu'erhai, Huanghutai, and others—over thirty thousand horsemen—who lined up along the Liao River, assaulted Dongchang Fort, and pushed inland as far as Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 成梁遣諸將分屯要害以遏之，而親提銳卒，出塞二百餘里，直搗圜山。

translations.literal: Chengliang sent his generals to garrison key points separately to block them, while he personally led crack troops more than two hundred li beyond the border in a direct strike at Yuanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang posted his generals at the critical passes to hold the enemy while he personally led elite troops more than two hundred li beyond the border in a straight thrust at Yuanshan.

sentences.zh: 斬首八百四十，及其長九人，獲馬千二百匹。

translations.literal: Eight hundred forty heads were cut off, along with nine of their leaders, and twelve hundred horses were captured.
translations.idiomatic: He took eight hundred forty heads, nine enemy leaders, and twelve hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 敵聞之，皆倉皇走出塞。

translations.literal: When the enemy heard of this, they all fled the border in panic.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the raiders, they all fled beyond the border in disarray.

sentences.zh: 論功，封甯遠伯，歲祿八百石。

translations.literal: His merit was assessed and he was enfeoffed as Earl of Ningyuan with an annual stipend of eight hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was enfeoffed as Earl of Ningyuan with an annual stipend of eight hundred piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 是時，土蠻數求貢市，關吏不許，大恨。

translations.literal: At this time Tümen repeatedly sought tributary trade, but the border officials would not permit it, and he harbored deep resentment.
translations.idiomatic: By then Tümen had repeatedly asked to trade at the border markets, but the gate officers refused him, and his resentment ran deep.

sentences.zh: 七年十月，復以四萬騎自前屯錦川營深入。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the seventh year he again advanced in depth with forty thousand horsemen from Qiantun and the Jinchuan camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year seven he again plunged deep into Ming territory with forty thousand horsemen from Qiantun and the Jinchuan camp.

sentences.zh: 成梁命諸將堅壁，自督參將楊粟等遏其沖。

translations.literal: Chengliang ordered his generals to hold the walls firmly while he personally directed Regional Vice Commander Yang Su and others to block the enemy's thrust.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang ordered his officers to stand firm behind the walls while he personally led Regional Vice Commander Yang Su and others to block the enemy's main thrust.

sentences.zh: 會戚繼光亦來援，敵遂退。

translations.literal: Qi Jiguang also came to the relief, and the enemy thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Jiguang arrived with reinforcements as well, and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 俄又與速把亥合壁紅土城，聲言入海州，而分兵入錦、義。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he joined Subanhai to encamp at Hongtu Fort, declaring that they would enter Haizhou while detaching troops to invade Jinzhou and Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he joined Subanhai in camp at Hongtu Fort, claiming they would strike Haizhou while detachments pushed into Jinzhou and Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 成梁逾塞二百餘里，直抵紅土城，擊敗之，獲首功四百七十有奇。

translations.literal: Chengliang went more than two hundred li beyond the border, advanced straight to Hongtu Fort, defeated them, and took more than four hundred seventy severed heads for merit.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang marched more than two hundred li beyond the border, struck Hongtu Fort head-on, routed the enemy, and claimed more than four hundred seventy heads.

sentences.zh: 迤東都督王兀堂故通市寬奠，後參將徐國輔弟國臣強抑市價，兀堂乃與趙鎖羅骨數遣零騎侵邊。

translations.literal: Wang Wutang, regional commander of eastern Liaodong, had formerly traded at Kuandian; later Regional Vice Commander Xu Guofu's younger brother Guochen forcibly suppressed market prices, whereupon Wutang, together with Zhao Suoluogu, repeatedly sent scattered horsemen to raid the border.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wutang, regional commander of eastern Liaodong, had long traded at Kuandian, but when Regional Vice Commander Xu Guofu's brother Guochen forced down market prices, Wutang joined Zhao Suoluogu in sending small parties of horsemen to harass the border again and again.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，以六百騎犯靉陽及黃岡嶺，指揮王宗義戰死。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year, with six hundred horsemen he attacked Aiyang and Huanggangling; Commander Wang Zongyi died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The next March he struck Aiyang and Huanggangling with six hundred horsemen; Commander Wang Zongyi was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 復以千餘騎從永奠入，成梁擊走之。

translations.literal: Again with more than a thousand horsemen he entered from Yongdian; Chengliang attacked and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: He returned with more than a thousand horsemen through Yongdian, but Chengliang beat him back.

sentences.zh: 追出塞二百里。

translations.literal: The pursuit went two hundred li beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit carried two hundred li beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 敵以騎卒拒，而步卒登山鼓噪。

translations.literal: The enemy used cavalry to resist, while infantry climbed the hills and beat drums and shouted.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy met him with cavalry while infantry took the heights, beating drums and shouting.

sentences.zh: 成梁大敗之，斬首七百五十，盡毀其營壘。

translations.literal: Chengliang inflicted a great defeat on them, cut off seven hundred fifty heads, and completely destroyed their camps and ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang routed them utterly, took seven hundred fifty heads, and destroyed their camps to the last.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，並錄紅土城功，予成梁世襲。

translations.literal: When news of the victory arrived, the merit at Hongtu Fort was also recorded and Chengliang was granted hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, the Hongtu Fort campaign was credited as well and Chengliang received a hereditary grant.

sentences.zh: 其秋，兀堂復犯寬奠，副將姚大節擊破之。

translations.literal: That autumn, Wutang again attacked Kuandian; Vice Commander Yao Dajie defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Wutang struck Kuandian again and was broken by Vice Commander Yao Dajie.

sentences.zh: 兀堂由是不振。

translations.literal: From this Wutang did not recover his strength.
translations.idiomatic: After that Wutang never regained his former power.

sentences.zh: 土蠻數侵邊不得志，忿甚，益征諸部兵分犯錦、義及右屯、大淩河。

translations.literal: Tümen had raided the border repeatedly without success and was deeply resentful; he further levied troops from the various tribes and sent them in separate columns against Jinzhou, Yizhou, Youdun, and the Greater Ling River.
translations.idiomatic: Tümen had raided again and again without success and burned with resentment; he mustered men from the other tribes and sent them in separate columns against Jinzhou, Yizhou, Youdun, and the Greater Ling River.

sentences.zh: 以城堡堅，不可克，而成梁及薊鎮兵亦集，乃引去。

translations.literal: Because the castles and forts were strong and could not be taken, and Chengliang and the troops of Jizhen had also gathered, they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The walled towns proved too strong to crack, and with Chengliang and the Jizhen forces massing against them, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 無何，復以二萬餘騎從大鎮堡入攻錦州。

translations.literal: Before long, with more than twenty thousand horsemen they entered through Dazhen Fort and attacked Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they returned with more than twenty thousand horsemen, entering through Dazhen Fort to assault Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 參將熊朝臣固守，而遣部將周之望、王應榮出戰，頗有斬獲。

translations.literal: Regional Vice Commander Xiong Chaochen held firm while sending subordinate generals Zhou Zhiwang and Wang Yingrong out to fight, with considerable kills and captures.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Vice Commander Xiong Chaochen held the defenses while sending his lieutenants Zhou Zhiwang and Wang Yingrong out to fight, and they took a fair number of heads.

sentences.zh: 矢盡，皆戰死。

translations.literal: When their arrows were exhausted, all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When their arrows ran out, both were killed in action.

sentences.zh: 敵乃分掠小淩河、松山、杏山。

translations.literal: The enemy then divided to plunder the Lesser Ling River, Songshan, and Xingshan.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy then split up to loot along the Lesser Ling River and at Songshan and Xingshan.

sentences.zh: 成梁馳援，始出境。

translations.literal: Chengliang galloped to the relief, and only then did they leave the border.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang raced to relieve them, and only then did the raiders withdraw beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，土蠻復與黑石炭，大、小委正，卜言台周，腦毛大，黃台吉，以兒鄧，暖兔，拱兔，炒戶兒聚兵塞下，謀入廣寧。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year, Tümen again joined Heishitan, Daweizheng, Xiaoweizheng, Buyan Taiju, Naomao Da, Huang Taiji, Yierdeng, Nuantu, Gongtu, and Chaohu'er to mass troops below the pass, plotting to enter Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year nine, Tümen again joined Heishitan, the Daweizheng and Xiaoweizheng brothers, Buyan Taiju, Naomao Da, Huang Taiji, Yierdeng, Nuantu, Gongtu, and Chaohu'er to gather an army below the pass, intending to break into Guangning.

sentences.zh: 成梁帥輕騎從大寧堡出。

translations.literal: Chengliang led light cavalry out from Daning Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang led light cavalry out through Daning Fort.

sentences.zh: 去塞四百餘里，至襖郎兔大戰。

translations.literal: More than four hundred li from the border, he fought a great battle at Aolangtu.
translations.idiomatic: More than four hundred li beyond the border he fought a major battle at Aolangtu.

sentences.zh: 自辰迄未，敵不支，敗走。

translations.literal: From the chen hour until the wei hour, the enemy could not hold and fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: From morning until mid-afternoon the enemy gave way and fled in defeat.

sentences.zh: 官軍將還，敵來追。

translations.literal: As the government troops were about to return, the enemy came in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: As the Ming forces prepared to withdraw, the enemy gave chase.

sentences.zh: 成梁逆擊，且戰且行。

translations.literal: Chengliang met them in counterattack, fighting as he marched.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang turned to meet them, fighting as he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 先後斬首三百四十，及其長八人。

translations.literal: In all three hundred forty heads were cut off, along with eight of their leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after, three hundred forty heads were taken, along with eight enemy leaders.

sentences.zh: 錄功，增歲祿百石，世廕一等。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded; his annual stipend was increased by one hundred piculs and his hereditary enfeoffment was raised one grade.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were recorded, his annual stipend was raised by one hundred piculs, and his hereditary rank advanced one step.

sentences.zh: 四月，黑石炭、以兒鄧、小歹青、卜言兔入遼陽。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Heishitan, Yierdeng, Xiaodaiqing, and Buyantu entered Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Heishitan, Yierdeng, Xiaodaiqing, and Buyantu raided into Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 副將曹簠追至長安堡，遇伏，失千總陳鵬以下三百十七人，馬死者四百六十匹，遂大掠人畜而去。

translations.literal: Vice Commander Cao Lin pursued as far as Chang'an Fort, met an ambush, and lost Battalion Commander Chen Peng and three hundred seventeen men below him; four hundred sixty horses died, and the enemy then plundered people and livestock on a great scale and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commander Cao Lin pursued them to Chang'an Fort, walked into an ambush, and lost Battalion Commander Chen Peng and three hundred seventeen men; four hundred sixty horses were killed, after which the enemy looted people and livestock on a vast scale and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 簠等下吏，成梁不問。

translations.literal: Lin and the others were handed over to the judicial authorities; Chengliang made no inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Lin and his officers were turned over to the courts, but Chengliang did not pursue the matter.

sentences.zh: 十月，土蠻復連速把亥等十余萬騎攻圍廣寧，不克，轉掠團山堡、盤山驛及十三山驛，攻義州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Tümen again joined Subanhai and others with more than one hundred thousand horsemen to besiege Guangning; failing to take it, they turned to plunder Tuanshan Fort, Panshan Post, and the Thirteen Mountains Post, and attacked Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Tümen again united with Subanhai and others—over one hundred thousand horsemen—to besiege Guangning; when they could not take it, they turned to raid Tuanshan Fort, Panshan Post, and the Thirteen Mountains Post, and assaulted Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 成梁禦卻之。

translations.literal: Chengliang repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang drove them back.

sentences.zh: 十年三月，速把亥率弟炒花、子卜言兔入犯義州。

translations.literal: In the third month of the tenth year, Subanhai led his younger brother Chaohua and his son Buyantu to invade Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year ten, Subanhai led his brother Chaohua and his son Buyantu in an attack on Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 成梁禦之鎮夷堡，設伏待之。

translations.literal: Chengliang met them at Zhenyi Fort and set an ambush to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang met them at Zhenyi Fort and laid an ambush.

sentences.zh: 速把亥入，參將李平胡射中其脅，墜馬，蒼頭李有名前斬之。

translations.literal: When Subanhai entered, Regional Vice Commander Li Pinghu shot him in the flank; he fell from his horse, and the servant Li Youming stepped forward and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Subanhai rode in, Regional Vice Commander Li Pinghu shot him in the side; he fell from his horse, and Li Youming, a household retainer, rushed forward and cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 寇大奔，追馘百餘級。

translations.literal: The raiders fled in great disorder; the pursuit took more than one hundred severed heads.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy broke and fled; the pursuit yielded more than one hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 炒花等慟哭去。

translations.literal: Chaohua and the others departed wailing in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Chaohua and the others withdrew, mourning loudly.

sentences.zh: 速把亥為遼左患二十年，至是死。

translations.literal: Subanhai had been a scourge in eastern Liaodong for twenty years; at this he died.
translations.idiomatic: Subanhai had plagued eastern Liaodong for twenty years; now he was dead.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，詔賜甲第京師，世廕錦衣指揮使。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and ordered that a fine mansion in the capital be granted him, with hereditary enfeoffment as commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and granted him a grand house in the capital, with hereditary rank as commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 初，王杲死，其子阿台走依王台長子虎兒罕。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wang Gao died, his son Atai fled to rely on Wang Tai's eldest son Hurhan.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Gao's death, his son Atai had fled to the protection of Wang Tai's eldest son Hurhan.

sentences.zh: 以王台獻其父，嘗欲報之。

translations.literal: Because Wang Tai had presented his father for execution, he had long wished to take revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wang Tai had handed his father over for execution, he had long wanted revenge.

sentences.zh: 王台死，虎兒罕勢衰，阿台遂附北關合攻虎兒罕。

translations.literal: When Wang Tai died, Hurhan's power declined, and Atai thereupon joined the Northern Pass faction to attack Hurhan jointly.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Tai died and Hurhan's power waned, Atai threw in with the Northern Pass clans to attack Hurhan together.

sentences.zh: 又數犯孤山、汛河。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly attacked Gushan and the Xun River.
translations.idiomatic: He also raided Gushan and the Xun River again and again.

sentences.zh: 成梁出塞，遇于曹子穀，斬首一千有奇，獲馬五百。

translations.literal: Chengliang went beyond the border and met him at Caozigu Valley, cutting off more than one thousand heads and capturing five hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang marched beyond the border and met him at Caozigu Valley, taking more than a thousand heads and five hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 阿台復糾阿海連兵入，抵瀋陽城南渾河，大掠去。

translations.literal: Atai again rallied Ahai to join forces and enter, reaching the Hun River south of Shenyang city, and departed after great plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Atai again joined Ahai in a raid that reached the Hun River south of Shenyang and withdrew after heavy looting.

sentences.zh: 成梁從撫順出塞百餘里，火攻古勒塞，射死阿台。

translations.literal: Chengliang went out from Fushun more than one hundred li beyond the border, attacked Gule stockade with fire, and shot Atai dead.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang marched from Fushun more than a hundred li beyond the border, burned Gule stockade, and shot Atai dead.

sentences.zh: 連破阿海寨，擊殺之，獻馘二千三百。

translations.literal: He stormed Ahai's stockades in succession, killed him in battle, and presented two thousand three hundred severed heads.
translations.idiomatic: He overran Ahai's camps in succession, killed him in battle, and reported two thousand three hundred heads taken.

sentences.zh: 杲部遂滅。

translations.literal: Gao's faction was thereby destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Gao's following was thus wiped out.

sentences.zh: 錄功，增歲祿百石，世廕指揮僉事。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded; his annual stipend was increased by one hundred piculs and hereditary enfeoffment as assistant commander was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were recorded, his stipend was raised by one hundred piculs, and his heir was enfeoffed as assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 北關清佳砮、楊吉砮素仇南關。

translations.literal: Qinggianu and Yanggianu of the Northern Pass had long been enemies of the Southern Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Qinggianu and Yanggianu of the Northern Pass had long feuded with the Southern Pass clans.

sentences.zh: 王台沒，屢侵台季子猛骨孛羅，且藉土蠻、暖兔、慌忽太兵侵邊境。

translations.literal: When Wang Tai died, they repeatedly encroached on his youngest son Menggu Boluo, and also borrowed the forces of Tümen, Nuantu, and Huanghutai to raid the border.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Tai's death they repeatedly harassed his youngest son Menggu Boluo and also used Tümen, Nuantu, and Huanghutai to strike the border.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，巡撫李松使備禦霍九皋許之貢市。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year, Grand Coordinator Li Song had Battalion Commander Huo Jiugao permit them tributary trade.
translations.idiomatic: That December Grand Coordinator Li Song had Battalion Commander Huo Jiugao grant them permission to trade at the tribute markets.

sentences.zh: 清佳砮、楊吉砮率二千餘騎詣鎮北關謁。

translations.literal: Qinggianu and Yanggianu led more than two thousand horsemen to Zhenbei Pass to pay their respects.
translations.idiomatic: Qinggianu and Yanggianu came to Zhenbei Pass with more than two thousand horsemen to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 松、九皋見其兵盛，譙讓之，則以三百騎入。

translations.literal: Song and Jiugao, seeing their forces were strong, rebuked them, whereupon they entered with only three hundred horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Song and Jiugao, alarmed by the size of their force, upbraided them until they agreed to enter with only three hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 松先伏甲於旁，約二人不受撫則砲舉甲起。

translations.literal: Song had first hidden armored troops nearby, agreeing that if the two men would not submit to pacification, the cannon would fire and the troops would rise.
translations.idiomatic: Song had already hidden armored troops nearby on the understanding that if the two leaders refused submission, a cannon shot would signal the ambush to rise.

sentences.zh: 頃之，二人抵關，據鞍不遜，松叱之，九皋麾使下，其徒遽拔刀擊九皋，並殺侍卒十餘人。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the two men reached the pass, sat their saddles insolently, and were shouted at by Song; Jiugao gestured for them to dismount, whereupon their followers suddenly drew swords and struck Jiugao, also killing more than ten attendant soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the two leaders reached the pass and remained mounted in defiance; Song rebuked them, and when Jiugao ordered them to dismount their men suddenly drew swords and attacked Jiugao, killing more than ten of his attendants as well.

sentences.zh: 於是軍中砲鳴，伏盡起，擊斬二人並其從騎，與清佳砮子兀孫孛羅、楊吉砮子哈兒哈麻盡殲焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the army's cannon sounded, the ambush troops all rose, struck and beheaded the two men and their mounted followers, and completely annihilated Qinggianu's son Wusun Boluo and Yanggianu's son Harhama.
translations.idiomatic: At that the cannon fired, the hidden troops sprang up, killed the two leaders and their escort, and wiped out Qinggianu's son Wusun Boluo and Yanggianu's son Harhama as well.

sentences.zh: 成梁聞砲，急出塞，擊其留騎，斬首千五百有奇。

translations.literal: Hearing the cannon, Chengliang hastened beyond the border and attacked their remaining horsemen, cutting off more than one thousand five hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the cannon, Chengliang rushed beyond the border and fell on the horsemen left behind, taking more than fifteen hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 余眾刑白馬，攢刀，誓永受約束，乃旋師。

translations.literal: The remaining men sacrificed a white horse, piled up knives, and swore to abide by restraint forever; only then did the army withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors sacrificed a white horse, piled their knives in pledge, and swore perpetual obedience before the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 錄功，增歲祿二百石，改前廕指揮僉事為錦衣衛指揮使。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded; his annual stipend was increased by two hundred piculs, and the previous hereditary enfeoffment as assistant commander was changed to commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were recorded, his stipend was raised by two hundred piculs, and his heir's hereditary rank was upgraded from assistant commander to commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 方成梁之出塞也，炒花等以數萬騎入蒲河及大寧堡。

translations.literal: Just as Chengliang was going beyond the border, Chaohua and others entered Puhe and Daning Fort with tens of thousands of horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: While Chengliang was out beyond the border, Chaohua and others swept into Puhe and Daning Fort with tens of thousands of horsemen.

sentences.zh: 將士防禦六日，始出塞。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers defended for six days before the enemy left the border.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison held them off for six days before they withdrew beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 十三年二月，把兔兒欲報父速把亥之怨，偕從父炒花、姑婿花大糾西部以兒鄧等以數萬騎入掠瀋陽。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirteenth year, Batu'er wished to avenge his father Subanhai; together with his uncle Chaohua and his aunt's husband Huada he rallied Yierdeng and others of the western tribes, and with tens of thousands of horsemen entered to plunder Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year thirteen, Batu'er sought revenge for his father Subanhai; with his uncle Chaohua and his aunt's husband Huada he rallied Yierdeng and other western leaders and swept into Shenyang with tens of thousands of horsemen.

sentences.zh: 既退，駐牧遼河，聲犯開原、鐵嶺。

translations.literal: After withdrawing, they encamped and pastured along the Liao River, declaring they would attack Kaiyuan and Tieling.
translations.idiomatic: After pulling back they camped along the Liao River, threatening Kaiyuan and Tieling.

sentences.zh: 成梁與巡撫李松潛為浮橋濟師，逾塞百五十里，疾掩其帳。

translations.literal: Chengliang and Grand Coordinator Li Song secretly built a pontoon bridge to ferry the army across, went one hundred fifty li beyond the border, and swiftly surrounded their tents.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang and Grand Coordinator Li Song secretly threw a pontoon bridge across the river, marched a hundred fifty li beyond the border, and fell swiftly on the enemy camp.

sentences.zh: 寇已先覺，整眾逆戰。

translations.literal: The raiders had already detected them, rallied their forces, and met them in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy had already sensed the move, formed up, and met them in battle.

sentences.zh: 成梁為疊陣，親督前陣擊，而松以後陣繼之，斬首八百有奇。

translations.literal: Chengliang formed echeloned ranks, personally directed the front rank in the attack, and Song followed with the rear rank; more than eight hundred heads were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang deployed in echelon, led the front line himself, and Song brought up the rear; they took more than eight hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，增歲祿百石，改廕錦衣指揮使為都指揮使。

translations.literal: When news of the victory arrived, his annual stipend was increased by one hundred piculs and hereditary enfeoffment as commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard was changed to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, his stipend rose by one hundred piculs and his heir's hereditary rank was upgraded from Embroidered Uniform Guard commander to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，敵犯瀋陽，伏精騎塞下，誘官軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year the enemy attacked Shenyang, hid elite cavalry below the pass, and lured the government troops.
translations.idiomatic: That May the enemy struck Shenyang, hiding picked cavalry below the pass to bait the Ming forces.

sentences.zh: 遊擊韓元功追襲之，敗死。

translations.literal: Mobile Corps Commander Han Yuangong pursued and attacked them, was defeated, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile Corps Commander Han Yuangong gave chase, was ambushed, and killed.

sentences.zh: 閏九月，諸部長復犯蒲河，殺裨將數人，大剽掠，而西部銀燈亦窺遼、瀋。

translations.literal: In the intercalary ninth month the tribal chieftains again attacked Puhe, killed several subordinate generals, and plundered on a great scale, while the westerner Yindeng also watched for chances at Liaoyang and Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary ninth month the chieftains raided Puhe again, killed several junior officers, and looted heavily, while the western leader Yindeng also probed Liaoyang and Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 成梁令部將李平胡出塞三百五十里，搗破銀燈營，斬首一百八級。

translations.literal: Chengliang ordered subordinate general Li Pinghu to go three hundred fifty li beyond the border, storm Yindeng's camp, and cut off one hundred eight heads.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang sent Li Pinghu three hundred fifty li beyond the border to smash Yindeng's camp and take one hundred eight heads.

sentences.zh: 諸部長聞之，始引去。

translations.literal: When the various chieftains heard of this, they then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the other chieftains heard of it, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十四年二月，士蠻部長一克灰正糾把兔兒、炒花、花大等三萬騎，約土蠻諸子共馳遼陽挾賞。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourteenth year, Tümen's chieftain Yikehuizheng rallied Batu'er, Chaohua, Huada, and others—thirty thousand horsemen—and arranged with Tümen's sons to ride together to Liaoyang to extort rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year fourteen, Tümen's chieftain Yikehuizheng mustered Batu'er, Chaohua, Huada, and others—thirty thousand horsemen—and agreed with Tümen's sons to ride on Liaoyang to demand payment.

sentences.zh: 成梁偵得之，率副將楊燮，參將李甯、李興、孫守廉以輕騎出鎮邊堡。

translations.literal: Chengliang learned of it through reconnaissance and led Vice Commander Yang Xie and Regional Vice Commanders Li Ning, Li Xing, and Sun Shoulian with light cavalry out from Zhenbian Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang learned of the plan through scouts and led Vice Commander Yang Xie and Regional Vice Commanders Li Ning, Li Xing, and Sun Shoulian with light cavalry out of Zhenbian Fort.

sentences.zh: 晝伏夜行二百餘里，至可哥毋林。

translations.literal: They hid by day and marched by night for more than two hundred li, reaching Kegewulin.
translations.idiomatic: They hid by day, marched by night for more than two hundred li, and reached Kegewulin.

sentences.zh: 大風雷，敵不覺。

translations.literal: There was a great wind and thunder; the enemy did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: A violent storm masked their approach, and the enemy never noticed.

sentences.zh: 既至，風日晴朗，敵大驚，發矢如雨。

translations.literal: When they arrived, the wind and sun were clear; the enemy was greatly alarmed and loosed arrows like rain.
translations.idiomatic: When they struck, the sky had cleared; the enemy panicked and loosed arrows like rain.

sentences.zh: 將士冒死陷陣，獲首功九百，斬其長二十四人。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers braved death and broke into the enemy ranks, taking nine hundred heads for merit and killing twenty-four of their leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men charged at the risk of their lives, claiming nine hundred heads and killing twenty-four enemy leaders.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，敵七八萬騎犯鎮夷諸堡，閱五日始去。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year, seventy or eighty thousand enemy horsemen attacked the forts around Zhenyi and did not leave until five days had passed.
translations.idiomatic: That October seventy or eighty thousand horsemen assaulted the forts around Zhenyi and did not withdraw for five days.

sentences.zh: 十五年春，東西部連營入犯。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifteenth year, the eastern and western tribes joined camps and invaded.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year fifteen the eastern and western tribes joined forces and invaded together.

sentences.zh: 其秋八月，復以七八萬騎犯鎮夷堡。

translations.literal: That autumn in the eighth month they again attacked Zhenyi Fort with seventy or eighty thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, in the eighth month, they returned with seventy or eighty thousand horsemen against Zhenyi Fort.

sentences.zh: 十月，把漢大成糾土蠻十萬騎由鎮夷、大清二堡入，數日始出。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Bahandacheng rallied one hundred thousand of Tümen's horsemen and entered through Zhenyi and Daqing forts; several days passed before they left.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Bahandacheng gathered one hundred thousand of Tümen's horsemen and entered through Zhenyi and Daqing; they did not withdraw for several days.

sentences.zh: 北關既被創，後清佳砮子卜寨與楊吉砮子那林孛羅漸強盛，數與南關虎兒罕子歹商構兵。

translations.literal: After the Northern Pass had been wounded, Qinggianu's son Bozhai and Yanggianu's son Nalin Boluo gradually grew powerful and repeatedly joined with Hurhan's son Daishang of the Southern Pass to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: After the Northern Pass clans had been crippled, Qinggianu's son Bozhai and Yanggianu's son Nalin Boluo grew steadily stronger and repeatedly allied with Hurhan's son Daishang of the Southern Pass for war.

sentences.zh: 成梁以南關勢弱，謀討北關以輔翊之。

translations.literal: Because the Southern Pass was weak in power, Chengliang planned to punish the Northern Pass in order to support and assist it.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the Southern Pass weakened, Chengliang planned to strike the Northern Pass to bolster it.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，率師直搗其巢。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the following year he led his army straight to storm their nest.
translations.idiomatic: The next May he led his army straight against their stronghold.

sentences.zh: 卜寨走，與那林孛羅合，憑城守。

translations.literal: Bozhai fled, joined Nalin Boluo, and relied on the city to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhai fled, joined Nalin Boluo, and held the walled town.

sentences.zh: 城四重，攻之不下。

translations.literal: The city had four rings of walls and could not be taken by assault.
translations.idiomatic: The town had four rings of walls and resisted assault.

sentences.zh: 用巨砲擊之，碎其外郛，遂拔二城，斬馘五百餘級。

translations.literal: They used great cannon against it, shattered the outer suburbs, then took two cities and cut off more than five hundred severed heads.
translations.idiomatic: They battered the outer walls with heavy cannon, took two towns, and claimed more than five hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 卜寨等請降，設誓不復叛，乃班師。

translations.literal: Bozhai and the others asked to surrender, swore oaths not to rebel again, and only then did the army withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhai and the others sued for peace, swore not to rebel again, and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十七年三月，敵犯義州，復入太平堡，把總硃永壽等一軍盡沒。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventeenth year the enemy attacked Yizhou, again entered Taiping Fort, and Company Commander Zhu Yongshou's entire force was wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year seventeen the enemy struck Yizhou, broke into Taiping Fort, and Company Commander Zhu Yongshou's whole detachment was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 九月，腦毛大合白洪大、長昂三萬騎復犯平虜堡，備禦李有年、把總馮文升皆戰死，成梁選鋒沒者數百人。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Naomao Da joined Baihong Da and Chang'ang with thirty thousand horsemen and again attacked Pinglu Fort; Battalion Commander Li Younian and Company Commander Feng Wensheng both died in battle, and several hundred of Chengliang's assault troops perished.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Naomao Da, Baihong Da, and Chang'ang struck Pinglu Fort again with thirty thousand horsemen; Battalion Commander Li Younian and Company Commander Feng Wensheng were killed, and several hundred of Chengliang's picked troops died as well.

sentences.zh: 敵大掠瀋陽蒲河、榆林，八日始去。

translations.literal: The enemy plundered Shenyang, Puhe, and Yulin on a great scale and did not leave until eight days had passed.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy looted Shenyang, Puhe, and Yulin for eight days before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，卜言台周，黃台吉，大、小委正結西部叉漢塔塔兒五萬余騎復深入遼、瀋、海、蓋。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year, Buyan Taiju, Huang Taiji, Daweizheng, and Xiaoweizheng joined the westerner Chahantatar with more than fifty thousand horsemen and again penetrated deeply into Liaoyang, Shenyang, Haizhou, and Gaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next February Buyan Taiju, Huang Taiji, the Daweizheng and Xiaoweizheng brothers, and the western leader Chahantatar united more than fifty thousand horsemen and again plunged deep into Liaoyang, Shenyang, Haizhou, and Gaizhou.

sentences.zh: 成梁潛遣兵出塞襲之，遇伏，死者千人。

translations.literal: Chengliang secretly sent troops beyond the border to strike them, met an ambush, and a thousand men died.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang secretly sent troops beyond the border to hit them, walked into an ambush, and lost a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 成梁乃報首功二百八十，得增祿廕。

translations.literal: Chengliang then reported two hundred eighty heads for merit and received increased stipend and enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang nevertheless reported two hundred eighty heads and received a higher stipend and hereditary grant.

sentences.zh: 土蠻族弟士墨台豬借西部青把都、恰不慎及長昂、滾兔十萬騎深入海州。

translations.literal: Tümen's clansman brother Shimotai Zhu borrowed the westerner Qingbadu, Qiaobushen, and Chang'ang and Gunu with one hundred thousand horsemen to penetrate deeply into Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tümen's kinsman Shimotai Zhu, with the western leaders Qingbadu and Qiaobushen and with Chang'ang and Gunu, led one hundred thousand horsemen deep into Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 成梁不敢擊，縱掠數日而去。

translations.literal: Chengliang did not dare attack and let them plunder for several days before they departed.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang did not dare give battle and let them loot for several days before they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十九年閏三月，成梁乘給事侯先春閱視，謀邀搗巢功，使副將李甯等出鎮夷堡潛襲板升，殺二百八十人。

translations.literal: In the intercalary third month of the nineteenth year, while Supervising Secretary Hou Xianchun was conducting an inspection, Chengliang sought merit by planning a surprise strike on the enemy camp and had Vice Commander Li Ning and others leave Zhenyi Fort to raid Bansheng secretly, killing two hundred eighty men.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary third month of year nineteen, while Supervising Secretary Hou Xianchun was on an inspection tour, Chengliang schemed for a merit-granting raid and sent Vice Commander Li Ning and others from Zhenyi Fort to strike Bansheng by surprise, killing two hundred eighty men.

sentences.zh: 師還遇敵，死者數千人。

translations.literal: On the army's return they met the enemy and several thousand men died.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home they ran into the enemy and lost several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 成梁及總督蹇達不以聞。

translations.literal: Chengliang and Governor-General Jian Da did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang and Governor-General Jian Da kept the losses from the throne.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史胡克儉盡發其先後欺罔狀，語多侵政府。

translations.literal: Touring Censor Hu Kejian fully exposed his successive acts of deception; his language often impinged on the government.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Censor Hu Kejian laid bare his pattern of deceit, and his memorials often struck at the court itself.

sentences.zh: 疏雖不行，成梁由是不安於位。

translations.literal: Although the memorial was not acted upon, from this Chengliang was no longer secure in his post.
translations.idiomatic: Though the memorial was not adopted, Chengliang was no longer secure in his post.

sentences.zh: 及先春還朝，詆尤力，帝意頗動。

translations.literal: When Xianchun returned to court, his denunciations were especially forceful, and the emperor's mind was somewhat moved.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianchun returned to court his attacks were especially fierce, and the emperor began to waver.

sentences.zh: 成梁再疏辭疾，言者亦踵至。

translations.literal: Chengliang again memorialized to resign on grounds of illness, and critics also arrived one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang memorialized again to resign on grounds of illness, and critics piled on one after another.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，帝竟從御史張鶴鳴言，解成梁任，以甯遠伯奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year the emperor finally followed Censor Zhang Heming's advice, relieved Chengliang of his post, and made him Earl of Ningyuan attending court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: That November the emperor at last took Censor Zhang Heming's advice, removed Chengliang from command, and kept him at court as Earl of Ningyuan with no active duty.

sentences.zh: 明年，哱拜反寧夏，御史梅國楨請用成梁，給事中王德完持不可，乃寢。

translations.literal: The following year, when Pai Bai rebelled in Ningxia, Censor Mei Guozhen asked that Chengliang be employed; Supervising Secretary Wang Dewan held that this could not be done, and the proposal was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Pai Bai rebelled in Ningxia, Censor Mei Guozhen urged that Chengliang be recalled; Supervising Secretary Wang Dewan objected, and the proposal died.

sentences.zh: 成梁鎮遼二十二年，先後奏大捷者十，帝輒祭告郊廟，受廷臣賀，蟒衣金繒歲賜稠疊。

translations.literal: Chengliang governed Liaodong for twenty-two years; he reported great victories on ten occasions, and each time the emperor offered thanks at the suburban altars, received congratulations from court officials, and bestowed python robes and gold brocade year after year in thick succession.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang held Liaodong for twenty-two years and reported ten great victories; each time the emperor sacrificed at the suburban altars, accepted congratulations from the court, and showered him with python robes and gold brocade year after year.

sentences.zh: 邊帥武功之盛，二百年來未有也。

translations.literal: In the splendor of martial achievement among frontier commanders, nothing like it had been seen in two hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: No frontier commander in two hundred years had matched such a record of military glory.

sentences.zh: 其始銳意封拜，師出必捷，威振絕域。

translations.literal: At first he was keen on enfeoffment and rank; whenever his army went out it was victorious, and his prestige shook the outer regions.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was hungry for honors; his campaigns always succeeded, and his fame reached the farthest frontiers.

sentences.zh: 已而位望益隆，子弟盡列崇階，僕隸無不榮顯。

translations.literal: Afterward his position and reputation grew ever loftier; his sons and younger brothers all held exalted ranks, and even his servants and slaves were without exception honored and prominent.
translations.idiomatic: In time his standing rose ever higher; his sons and brothers filled the highest ranks, and even his servants rode on privilege.

sentences.zh: 貴極而驕，奢侈無度。

translations.literal: Having reached the pinnacle of honor he became arrogant, and his extravagance knew no bounds.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of his power he turned arrogant and spent without limit.

sentences.zh: 軍貲、馬價、鹽課、市賞，歲幹沒不貲，全遼商民之利盡籠入己。

translations.literal: Military funds, horse prices, salt levies, and market rewards—each year he embezzled sums beyond reckoning, and all the profits of merchants and commoners in Liaodong were drawn entirely into his own hands.
translations.idiomatic: Military funds, horse prices, salt levies, and market bounties—year after year he skimmed sums beyond counting, and monopolized every profit that traders and commoners in Liaodong might have made.

sentences.zh: 以是灌輸權門，結納朝士，中外要人，無不飽其重賕，為之左右。

translations.literal: With this he poured wealth into powerful families, cultivated ties with court officials, and none of the important men inside or outside the government failed to be filled with his heavy bribes and speak on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: With this wealth he bought off powerful families and courtiers alike; no influential figure inside or outside the government escaped his lavish bribes or failed to plead his cause.

sentences.zh: 每一奏捷，內自閣部，外自督撫而下，大者進官廕子，小亦增俸賚金。

translations.literal: Whenever he reported a victory, from the Grand Secretariat and ministries within to the governors and coordinators without and below, the greater were advanced in office and had sons enfeoffed, while the lesser also received increased salaries and bestowed gold.
translations.idiomatic: Every victory he reported brought rewards all down the line—from the Grand Secretariat to the frontier governors: the senior were promoted and their sons enfeoffed, the junior received raises and gold.

sentences.zh: 恩施優渥，震耀當世。

translations.literal: Favors and grace were lavish, dazzling the age.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial favor was lavish beyond measure, and his glory dazzled the age.

sentences.zh: 而其戰功率在塞外，易為緣飾。

translations.literal: Yet his battles were mostly beyond the border, where it was easy to embellish the record.
translations.idiomatic: Yet most of his fighting took place beyond the border, where accounts were easy to dress up.

sentences.zh: 若敵入內地，則以堅壁清野為詞，擁兵觀望；

translations.literal: If the enemy entered the interior, he took strengthening walls and clearing the countryside as his excuse and held his troops back to watch;
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy penetrated inland he cited the doctrine of strengthening walls and clearing the countryside while holding his troops back to watch;

sentences.zh: 甚或掩敗為功，殺良民冒級。

translations.literal: in extreme cases he concealed defeat as victory and killed innocent commoners to claim merit grades.
translations.idiomatic: and in the worst cases he turned defeat into victory and killed peaceful civilians to claim merit heads.

sentences.zh: 閣部共為蒙蔽，督撫、監司稍忤意，輒排去之，不得舉其法。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretariat and ministries together shielded him; if governors, coordinators, or surveillance commissioners slightly displeased him, he had them removed and they could not bring charges according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretariat and ministries shielded him together; any governor, coordinator, or surveillance commissioner who crossed him was driven out before he could be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 先後巡按陳登雲、許守恩廉得其殺降冒功狀，擬論奏之，為巡撫李松、顧養謙所沮止。

translations.literal: In succession the touring censors Chen Dengyun and Xu Shou'en investigated and obtained evidence of his killing those who surrendered and claiming false merit; they prepared memorials of accusation, but were blocked by Grand Coordinators Li Song and Gu Yangqian.
translations.idiomatic: Touring censors Chen Dengyun and Xu Shou'en in turn uncovered his practice of killing surrendering men and claiming false merit and prepared indictments, but Grand Coordinators Li Song and Gu Yangqian blocked them.

sentences.zh: 既而物議沸騰，御史硃應轂、給事中任應徵、僉事李琯交章抨擊。

translations.literal: Afterward public opinion boiled over; Censor Zhu Yinggu, Supervising Secretary Ren Yingzheng, and Vice Commissioner Li Guan submitted memorial after memorial attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long public outrage boiled over, and Censor Zhu Yinggu, Supervising Secretary Ren Yingzheng, and Vice Commissioner Li Guan bombarded the court with memorials against him.

sentences.zh: 事頗有跡，卒賴奧援，反詰責言者。

translations.literal: The matter quite had traces; in the end relying on hidden backing, they instead interrogated and blamed those who spoke.
translations.idiomatic: The charges had substance, yet thanks to powerful patrons at court, the accusers themselves were rebuked.

sentences.zh: 及申時行、許國、王錫爵相繼謝政，成梁失內主，遂以去位。

translations.literal: When Shen Shixing, Xu Guo, and Wang Xijue in succession resigned from office, Chengliang lost his inner patrons, and so resigned his post.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shen Shixing, Xu Guo, and Wang Xijue had left office in turn, Chengliang lost his protectors at court and was forced to step down.

sentences.zh: 成梁諸戰功率藉健兒。

translations.literal: Chengliang's several battles mostly relied on his valiant soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In most of his battles, Chengliang depended on his private corps of elite fighters.

sentences.zh: 其後健兒李平胡、李甯、李興、秦得倚、孫守廉輩皆富貴，擁專城。

translations.literal: Thereafter valiant soldiers such as Li Pinghu, Li Ning, Li Xing, Qin Deyi, and Sun Shoulian all grew wealthy and noble, each holding sole control of a walled city.
translations.idiomatic: Later those valiant soldiers—Li Pinghu, Li Ning, Li Xing, Qin Deyi, Sun Shoulian, and others—grew rich and powerful, each commanding a city of his own.

sentences.zh: 暮氣難振，又轉相掊克，士馬蕭耗。

translations.literal: Evening spirits were hard to revive; moreover they in turn extorted one another, and troops and horses withered away.
translations.idiomatic: The army had sunk into lethargy; the commanders preyed on one another, and men and horses dwindled away.

sentences.zh: 迨成梁去遼，十年之間更易八帥，邊備益弛。

translations.literal: When Chengliang left Liaodong, within ten years eight commanders were changed, and frontier preparations grew ever laxer.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengliang left Liaodong, eight commanders succeeded one another in a decade, and frontier defenses steadily decayed.

sentences.zh: 二十九年八月，馬林獲罪。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, eighth month, Ma Lin was found guilty of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year twenty-nine, Ma Lin was punished for an offense.

sentences.zh: 大學士沈一貫言成梁雖老，尚堪將兵。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan said that though Chengliang was old, he could still command troops.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan argued that despite his age, Chengliang remained fit to lead armies.

sentences.zh: 乃命再鎮遼東，年已七十有六矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was ordered to govern Liaodong again; he was already seventy-six years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore sent back to command Liaodong, though he was already seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 是時，土蠻、長昂及把兔兒已死，寇鈔漸稀。

translations.literal: At that time Tumen, Chang Ang, and Batuer were already dead, and border raids gradually grew rare.
translations.idiomatic: By then Tumen, Chang Ang, and Batuer had all died, and raids across the border grew infrequent.

sentences.zh: 而開原、廣寧之前復開馬、木二市。

translations.literal: Moreover, before Kaiyuan and Guangning, the horse and wood markets were reopened.
translations.idiomatic: The horse and timber markets were reopened near Kaiyuan and Guangning.

sentences.zh: 諸部耽市賞利，爭就款。

translations.literal: The various tribes were addicted to market rewards and profit, and vied to submit in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes coveted the profits of trade and competed to make peace.

sentences.zh: 以故成梁復鎮八年，遼左少事。

translations.literal: For this reason Chengliang governed again for eight years, and east of Liaodong had few incidents.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang therefore held command for another eight years, and eastern Liaodong saw little trouble.

sentences.zh: 以閱視敘勞，加至太傅。

translations.literal: On account of inspection tours and ordering of merit, he was advanced to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: After frontier inspections and merit reviews, he was promoted to Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 當萬曆初元時，兵部侍郎汪道昆閱邊，成梁獻議移建孤山堡于張其哈剌佃，險山堡於寬佃，沿江新安四堡於長佃、長嶺諸處，仍以孤山、險山二參將戍之，可拓地七八百里，益收耕牧之利。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wanli, Vice Minister of War Wang Daokun inspected the border; Chengliang offered a proposal to relocate Gushan Fort to Zhangqihala tuntian, Xianshan Fort to Kuantun, and along the river move the four forts of Xin'an to Changtun, Changling, and other places, still posting the two vice commanders of Gushan and Xianshan to garrison them—this could extend territory seven or eight hundred li and further gain the benefits of farming and herding.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli's first year, Vice Minister of War Wang Daokun toured the frontier. Chengliang proposed moving Gushan Fort to Zhangqihala tuntian, Xianshan Fort to Kuantun, and relocating the four Xin'an forts along the river to Changtun, Changling, and nearby sites, with vice commanders garrisoning Gushan and Xianshan—thereby opening seven or eight hundred li of land and reaping greater gains from agriculture and grazing.

sentences.zh: 道昆上於朝，報可。

translations.literal: Daokun submitted it to court; the reply was approval.
translations.idiomatic: Wang submitted the plan to court and received approval.

sentences.zh: 自是生聚日繁，至六萬四千餘戶。

translations.literal: From this population and settlement daily grew denser, reaching more than sixty-four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Settlers multiplied until the region held more than sixty-four thousand households.

sentences.zh: 及三十四年，成梁以地孤懸難守，與督、撫蹇達、趙楫建議棄之，盡徙居民于內地。

translations.literal: By year thirty-four, Chengliang on grounds that the land stood isolated and was hard to hold, together with the supreme commander and grand coordinator Jian Da and Zhao Ji proposed to abandon it, and completely moved the inhabitants into the interior.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-four, Chengliang joined Supreme Commander Jian Da and Grand Coordinator Zhao Ji in urging abandonment, citing the land's exposed position; all settlers were driven into the interior.

sentences.zh: 居民戀家室，則以大軍驅迫之，死者狼籍。

translations.literal: The inhabitants were attached to their homes and families; then with a great army they were driven and compelled, and the dead lay strewn about.
translations.idiomatic: The people clung to their homes; the army drove them out by force, and corpses littered the roads.

sentences.zh: 成梁等反以招復逃人功，增秩受賞。

translations.literal: Chengliang and others on the contrary took as merit the attracting back of fugitives, and were advanced in rank and received reward.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang and his colleagues were nonetheless rewarded with promotions for having "recalled fugitives."

sentences.zh: 兵科給事中宋一韓力言棄地非策。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Song Yihan of the Military Affairs Section strongly stated that abandoning territory was not a good policy.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Song Yihan of the military affairs section vehemently argued that abandoning the land was a fatal mistake.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史熊廷弼勘奏如一韓言，一韓復連章極論。

translations.literal: Touring Censor Xiong Tingbi investigated and memorialized as Yihan had said; Yihan again in linked memorials argued to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Censor Xiong Tingbi investigated and reported as Song Yihan had warned; Song Yihan followed with a series of impassioned memorials.

sentences.zh: 帝素眷成梁，悉留中不下。

translations.literal: The emperor had long favored Chengliang; he kept all memorials within and did not release them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, who had always favored Chengliang, suppressed every memorial and let none reach the open court.

sentences.zh: 久之卒，年九十。

translations.literal: After a long time he died, aged ninety.
translations.idiomatic: He died at last, aged ninety.

sentences.zh: 弟成材，參將。

translations.literal: His younger brother Chengcai was a vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chengcai held the rank of vice commander.

sentences.zh: 子如松、如柏、如楨、如樟、如梅皆總兵官；

translations.literal: Sons Rusong, Rubai, Ruzhen, Ruzhang, and Rumei were all regional commanders;
translations.idiomatic: His sons Rusong, Rubai, Ruzhen, Ruzhang, and Rumei all became regional commanders;

sentences.zh: 如梓、如梧、如桂、如楠亦皆至參將。

translations.literal: Ruzi, Ruwu, Rugui, and Runnan also all reached the rank of vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: Ruzi, Ruwu, Rugui, and Runnan rose to vice commander as well.

sentences.zh: 子 如松

translations.literal: Son: Rusong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rusong

sentences.zh: 如松，字子茂，成梁長子。

translations.literal: Rusong, styled Zimao, was Chengliang's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rusong, style name Zimao, was Chengliang's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 以父廕為都指揮同知，充甯遠伯勳衛。

translations.literal: Through his father's hereditary privilege he became vice commissioner of the regional military commission, and served as honorary guard of the Earl of Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's privilege he entered office as vice commissioner of the regional military commission and served in the hereditary guard of the Earl of Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 驍果敢戰，少從父諳兵機。

translations.literal: Fierce and brave, he dared fight; from youth following his father he became versed in military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and battle-hardened, he had learned the art of war at his father's side since boyhood.

sentences.zh: 再遷署都督僉事，為神機營右副將。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to acting vice commissioner of the chief military commission and became deputy commander of the Divine Engine Corps on the right.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting vice commissioner of the chief military commission and appointed deputy commander of the Divine Engine Corps.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十一年，出為山西總兵官。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Wanli he went out as regional commander of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year eleven he was appointed regional commander of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 給事中黃道瞻等數言如松父子不當並居重鎮，大學士申時行請保全之，乃召僉書右府。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Huang Daozhan and others repeatedly said that father and son Rusong ought not both to hold heavy frontier posts; Grand Secretary Shen Shixing asked that they be protected and preserved, and Rusong was summoned to serve as secretary in the right office of the military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Huang Daozhan and others protested that father and son should not hold major frontier commands together; Grand Secretary Shen Shixing interceded to protect him, and Rusong was recalled to a secretarial post in the right office of the military commission.

sentences.zh: 尋提督京城巡捕。

translations.literal: Soon he was made supreme commander of the capital's patrol and arrest duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed to direct the capital's patrol police.

sentences.zh: 給事中邵庶嘗劾如松及其弟副總兵如柏不法，且請稍抑，以全終始，不納。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Shao Shu once impeached Rusong and his younger brother, vice regional commander Rubai, for illegal conduct, and also asked that they be somewhat restrained to preserve their good endings to the end—this was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Shao Shu once impeached Rusong and his younger brother Rubai, vice regional commander, for misconduct and urged that their power be curbed for their own good; the plea was rejected.

sentences.zh: 十五年，復以總兵官鎮宣府。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he again served as regional commander garrisoning Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen he returned to Xuanfu as regional commander.

sentences.zh: 巡撫許守謙閱操，如松引坐與並。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Xu Shouqian reviewed troops on parade; Rusong led him to be seated side by side as equals.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Coordinator Xu Shouqian reviewed the troops on parade, Rusong insisted on seating him as an equal.

sentences.zh: 參政王學書卻之，語不相下，幾攘臂。

translations.literal: Administration Vice Commissioner Wang Xueshu declined this; words would not yield, and they nearly came to blows.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Wang Xueshu refused; the exchange grew heated and nearly came to blows.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史王之棟因劾如松驕橫，並詆學書，帝為兩奪其俸。

translations.literal: Touring Censor Wang Zhidong thereupon impeached Rusong for arrogant tyranny and also slandered Xueshu; the emperor for both deducted their salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Censor Wang Zhidong impeached Rusong for arrogance and criticized Xueshu as well; the emperor docked both men's salaries.

sentences.zh: 已復被論，給事中葉初春請改調之，乃命與山西李迎恩更鎮。

translations.literal: Afterward he was again criticized; Supervising Secretary Ye Chuchun asked that he be transferred elsewhere, and the order was made for him and Li Ying'en of Shanxi to exchange commands.
translations.idiomatic: Criticism mounted again; Supervising Secretary Ye Chuchun urged a transfer, and Rusong was ordered to swap posts with Li Ying'en of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 其後，軍政拾遺，給事中閱視，數遭論劾。

translations.literal: Afterward, military administration had oversights and remnants; supervising secretaries on inspection tours repeatedly subjected him to criticism and impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter lapses in military administration brought repeated impeachments from supervising secretaries on inspection tours.

sentences.zh: 帝終眷之，不為動，召僉書中府。

translations.literal: The emperor to the end favored him and was not moved; he was summoned to serve as secretary in the central office of the military commission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's favor never wavered; Rusong was recalled to a secretarial post in the central military commission.

sentences.zh: 二十年，哱拜反寧夏，御史梅國楨薦如松大將才，其弟如梅、如樟並年少英傑，宜令討賊。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Pai Bai rebelled in Ningxia; Censor Mei Guozhen recommended Rusong's great-general talent, and his younger brothers Rumei and Ruzhang were together young and heroic—they should be ordered to suppress the rebels.
