translations.idiomatic: In year twenty, when Pai Bai rebelled in Ningxia, Censor Mei Guozhen recommended Rusong as a commander of exceptional talent and urged that his young brothers Rumei and Ruzhang join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 乃命如松為提督陝西討逆軍務總兵官，即以國楨監之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Rusong was ordered to be supreme commander of Shaanxi for the suppression of rebels, with military affairs overall, regional commander, and Guozhen placed to supervise him.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong was appointed supreme commander of Shaanxi military affairs against the rebels, with Mei Guozhen as supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 武臣有提督，自如松始也。

translations.literal: Among military officials to have a supreme commander began with Rusong.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong was the first military officer to receive the title of supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 已命盡統遼東、宣府、大同、山西諸道援軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to command entirely the relief armies of the circuits of Liaodong, Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon placed in command of all relief forces from Liaodong, Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 六月抵寧夏。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he reached Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Ningxia in the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 如松以權任既重，不欲受總督制，事輒專行。

translations.literal: Rusong, his authority and responsibility already heavy, did not wish to be controlled by the governor-general and on affairs constantly acted on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong's authority was vast, and he resented taking orders from the governor-general; on nearly every matter he acted alone.

sentences.zh: 兵科許弘綱等以為非制，尚書石星亦言如松敕書受督臣節度，不得自專，帝乃下詔申飭。

translations.literal: Xu Honggang and others of the military affairs section held this contrary to regulation; Minister Shi Xing also said that Rusong's commission received the governor-general's direction and he could not act on his own; the emperor then issued an edict sternly admonishing him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Honggang and others protested that this violated precedent; Minister of War Shi Xing reminded the court that Rusong's commission required him to obey the governor-general; the emperor issued an edict rebuking him.

sentences.zh: 先是，諸將董一奎、麻貴等數攻城不下。

translations.literal: Earlier, the generals Dong Yikui, Ma Gui, and others had several times assaulted the city without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Dong Yikui, Ma Gui, and others had already assaulted the city several times without success.

sentences.zh: 如松至，攻益力。

translations.literal: When Rusong arrived, the assault grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong's arrival intensified the assault.

sentences.zh: 用布囊三萬，實以土，踐之登，為砲石所卻。

translations.literal: They used thirty thousand cloth bags, filled with earth, trampled them to ascend, but were repelled by cannon stones.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty thousand earth-filled sacks were piled to scale the walls, but cannon fire drove the attackers back.

sentences.zh: 如樟夜攀雲梯上，不克。

translations.literal: Ruzhang by night climbed cloud ladders to ascend but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Ruzhang led a night assault up scaling ladders but failed.

sentences.zh: 遊擊龔子敬提苗兵攻南關，如松乘勢將登，亦不克，乃決策水攻。

translations.literal: Mobile corps commander Gong Zijing led Miao troops to attack the south gate; Rusong seized the momentum and was about to ascend but also did not succeed, and then decided on a water attack.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile corps commander Gong Zijing attacked the south gate with Miao troops; Rusong pressed the assault but was likewise repulsed, and turned to flooding the city.

sentences.zh: 拜窘，遣養子克力蓋往勾套寇，如松令部將李寧追斬之。

translations.literal: Pai Bai in distress sent his adopted son Keligai to summon the Ordos tribes; Rusong ordered his subordinate commander Li Ning to pursue and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Pai Bai sent his adopted son Keligai to summon Ordos allies; Rusong sent Li Ning in pursuit, who caught and killed him.

sentences.zh: 已，套寇以萬余騎至張亮堡。

translations.literal: Already the Ordos tribes had arrived with more than ten thousand horsemen at Zhangliang Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Soon more than ten thousand Ordos horsemen reached Zhangliang Fort.

sentences.zh: 如松力戰，手斬士卒畏縮者，寇竟敗去。

translations.literal: Rusong fought fiercely, with his own hand beheading soldiers who shrank back in fear; the enemy in the end was defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong fought fiercely, personally executing troops who flinched; the raiders were routed.

sentences.zh: 水侵北關，城崩。

translations.literal: Water invaded the north gate and the wall collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Floodwaters breached the north gate and brought down the wall.

sentences.zh: 如松及蕭如薰等佯擊北關誘賊，而潛以銳師襲南關，攀雲梯而上。

translations.literal: Rusong and Xiao Ruxun and others feigned attacking the north gate to lure the rebels, while secretly with crack troops raided the south gate and climbed up on cloud ladders.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong and Xiao Ruxun staged a feint at the north gate while elite troops stormed the south wall on scaling ladders.

sentences.zh: 拜及子承恩自斬叛黨劉東暘、許朝乞貸死。

translations.literal: Pai Bai and his son Chengen themselves beheaded the rebel partisans Liu Dongyang and Xu Chao and begged that their lives be spared.
translations.idiomatic: Pai Bai and his son Chengen executed their lieutenants Liu Dongyang and Xu Chao and pleaded for their own lives.

sentences.zh: 於是如松先登，如薰及麻貴、劉承嗣等繼之，盡滅拜族。

translations.literal: Thereupon Rusong ascended first; Ruxun and Ma Gui, Liu Chengsi, and others followed, and Pai Bai's clan was utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong was first over the wall; Ruxun, Ma Gui, Liu Chengsi, and others followed, and Pai Bai's clan was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 錄功，進都督，世廕錦衣指揮同知。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded; he was advanced to regional commander-in-chief, with hereditary enfeoffment as vice commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were entered on the rolls; he was promoted to regional commander-in-chief, with hereditary rank as vice commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 會朝鮮倭患棘，詔如松提督薊、遼、保定、山東諸軍，克期東征。

translations.literal: It happened that Korea's Japanese trouble was acute; an edict ordered Rusong supreme commander of the armies of Ji, Liaodong, Baoding, and Shandong, with a set date for the eastern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Japanese invasion of Korea grew urgent; Rusong was ordered to command the armies of Ji, Liaodong, Baoding, and Shandong for an eastern campaign on a fixed schedule.

sentences.zh: 弟如柏、如梅並率師援剿。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Rubai and Rumei together led armies to aid in the suppression.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Rubai and Rumei marched with their own forces to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 如松新立功，氣益驕，與經略宋應昌不相下。

translations.literal: Rusong having newly achieved merit, his spirit grew ever prouder; he would not yield to Commissioner Song Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh from victory, Rusong grew insufferably arrogant and refused to defer to Commissioner Song Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 故事，大帥初見督師，甲胄庭謁，出易冠帶，始加禮貌。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a great commander first met the supervising commissioner, he wore armor and paid court obeisance in the courtyard; going out he changed to cap and belt, and only then were courtesies added.
translations.idiomatic: By custom a commander meeting his supervising commissioner for the first time appeared in armor to perform obeisance in the courtyard, then changed into formal dress before civilities were exchanged.

sentences.zh: 如松用監司謁督撫儀，素服側坐而已。

translations.literal: Rusong used the ceremony of a surveillance commissioner calling on a governor-coordinator—plain dress, seated to one side, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong greeted Song with the perfunctory ceremony a surveillance commissioner owed a governor—plain clothes and a seat to one side.

sentences.zh: 十二月，如松至軍，沈惟敬自倭歸，言倭酋行長願封，請退平壤迄西，以大同江為界。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Rusong reached the army; Shen Weijing returned from the Japanese and said the Wo chieftain Hideyoshi wished enfeoffment, asking to withdraw from Pyongyang westward with the Taedong River as boundary.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Rusong reached the front. Shen Weijing had returned from negotiations saying Hideyoshi sought investiture and offered to withdraw west of Pyongyang as far as the Taedong River.

sentences.zh: 如松叱惟敬憸邪，欲斬之。

translations.literal: Rusong rebuked Weijing as crafty and treacherous and wished to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong denounced Shen Weijing as a devious mediator and nearly had him executed.

sentences.zh: 參謀李應試曰：「藉惟敬紿倭封，而陰襲之，奇計也。」

translations.literal: Staff officer Li Yingshi said: "By borrowing Weijing to deceive the Wo with enfeoffment, while in secret striking them—it is a marvelous plan.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Li Yingshi said, "Use Shen Weijing to lure the Japanese with promises of investiture, then strike in secret—that is a brilliant stratagem.

sentences.zh: 如松以為然，乃置惟敬于營，誓師渡江。

translations.literal: Rusong thought it right, then placed Weijing in the camp and swore the army to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong agreed, kept Shen Weijing in camp, and led the army across the river after a solemn oath.

sentences.zh: 二十一年正月四日，師次肅寧館。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the first month of the twenty-first year, the army halted at Suning Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the first month, year twenty-one, the army encamped at Suning Lodge.

sentences.zh: 行長以為封使將至，遣牙將二十人來迎，如松檄遊擊李寧生縛之。

translations.literal: Hideyoshi thought investiture envoys were about to arrive and sent twenty junior generals to welcome them; Rusong ordered Mobile Corps Commander Li Ningsheng to bind them.
translations.idiomatic: Hideyoshi, expecting investiture envoys, sent twenty officers to welcome them; Rusong ordered Mobile Corps Commander Li Ningsheng to seize them.

sentences.zh: 倭猝起格鬥，僅獲三人，餘走還。

translations.literal: The Japanese suddenly rose to grapple and fight; only three were captured and the rest fled back.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese fought back; only three were taken, the rest escaped.

sentences.zh: 行長大駭，復遣所親信小西飛來謁，如松慰遣之。

translations.literal: Hideyoshi was greatly alarmed and again sent his trusted intimate Konishi Yukinaga to call on them; Rusong comforted and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Hideyoshi was shaken and sent his confidant Konishi Yukinaga; Rusong put him at ease and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 六日，次平壤。

translations.literal: On the sixth day they halted at Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth they reached Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 行長猶以為封使也，踔風月樓以待，群倭花衣夾道迎。

translations.literal: Hideyoshi still thought they were investiture envoys; he leaped to Moonlight Tower to wait, and the crowd of Japanese in flowered robes lined the road to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Hideyoshi still believed them to be investiture envoys; he waited at Moonlight Tower while Japanese officers in ceremonial robes lined the streets to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 如松分佈諸軍，抵平壤城，諸將逡巡未入，形大露，倭悉登陴拒守。

translations.literal: Rusong deployed the various armies and reached Pyongyang city; the generals hesitated and did not enter—their form was greatly exposed, and all the Japanese mounted the ramparts to resist and hold.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong deployed his forces before the city, but his generals hesitated at the gates; the ruse was exposed, and the Japanese manned the walls.

sentences.zh: 是夜，襲如柏營，擊卻之。

translations.literal: That night they raided Rubai's camp and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: That night they raided Rubai's camp but were driven off.

sentences.zh: 明旦，如松下令諸軍無割首級，攻圍缺東面。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day Rusong ordered the armies not to cut off heads and to attack surrounding the gap on the east face.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Rusong forbade his men to pursue heads for merit and ordered a concentrated assault on the east.

sentences.zh: 以倭素易朝鮮軍，令副將祖承訓詭為其裝，潛伏西南。

translations.literal: Because the Japanese habitually despised Korean troops, he ordered Vice Commander Zu Chengxun to disguise himself in their garb and lie in ambush to the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the Japanese held Korean troops in contempt, he sent Vice Commander Zu Chengxun's men forward disguised as Korean soldiers, lying in wait to the southwest.

sentences.zh: 令遊擊吳惟忠攻迄北牡丹峰。

translations.literal: He ordered Mobile Corps Commander Wu Weizhong to attack through to North Peony Peak on the north.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile Corps Commander Wu Weizhong was ordered to attack Peony Peak on the north.

sentences.zh: 而如松親提大軍直抵城下，攻其東南。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Rusong personally led the great army straight to below the city and attacked its southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong personally led the main force to the southeast wall.

sentences.zh: 倭砲矢如雨，軍少卻。

translations.literal: Japanese cannon and arrows fell like rain; the army slightly fell back.
translations.idiomatic: A storm of Japanese fire forced the army to give ground.

sentences.zh: 如松斬先退者以徇。

translations.literal: Rusong beheaded those who retreated first to display as warning.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong executed the first men to retreat as an example.

sentences.zh: 募死士，援鉤梯直上。

translations.literal: He recruited death-daring warriors who, supporting hook ladders, went straight up.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied volunteers who stormed the walls on grappling hooks.

sentences.zh: 倭方輕南面朝鮮軍，承訓等乃卸裝露明甲。

translations.literal: The Japanese were just then despising the south face's Korean army; Chengxun and others then removed their disguises and revealed bright armor.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese, still treating the southern force as Koreans, were stunned when Chengxun's men threw off their disguises and revealed Ming armor.

sentences.zh: 倭大驚，急分兵捍拒，如松已督副將楊元等軍自小西門先登，如柏等亦從大西門入。

translations.literal: The Japanese were greatly alarmed and hastily divided troops to resist; Rusong already had supervised Vice Commander Yang Yuan and others' army to ascend first from the Small West Gate, and Rubai and others also entered from the Great West Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Panicked, the Japanese divided their forces; Rusong had already led Yang Yuan's men over the Small West Gate, while Rubai entered through the Great West Gate.

sentences.zh: 火器併發，煙焰蔽空。

translations.literal: Fire weapons discharged together, smoke and flames covering the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Volleys of firearms filled the sky with smoke and flame.

sentences.zh: 惟忠中砲傷胸，猶奮呼督戰。

translations.literal: Weizhong was struck by cannon and wounded in the chest, yet still fiercely shouted and directed the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Weizhong took a cannonball to the chest yet continued shouting orders.

sentences.zh: 如松馬斃于砲，易馬馳，墮塹，躍而上，麾兵益進。

translations.literal: Rusong's horse was killed by cannon; he changed horses and galloped, fell into a moat, leaped up, and waved the army to press forward ever more.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong's horse was killed by cannon fire; he mounted another, fell into a moat, clawed his way out, and drove his men forward.

sentences.zh: 將士無不一當百，遂克之。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers were without exception one against a hundred, and so they captured it.
translations.idiomatic: His men fought as ten against one, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 獲首功千二百有奇。

translations.literal: Heads taken for merit reached more than twelve hundred.
translations.idiomatic: More than twelve hundred enemy heads were counted for merit.

sentences.zh: 倭退保風月樓。

translations.literal: The Japanese retreated to hold Moonlight Tower.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors fell back to Moonlight Tower.

sentences.zh: 夜半，行長渡大同江，遁還龍山。

translations.literal: At midnight Hideyoshi crossed the Taedong River and fled back to Ryongsan.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight Hideyoshi crossed the Taedong and fled to Ryongsan.

sentences.zh: 甯及參將查大受率精卒三千潛伏東江間道，復斬級三百六十。

translations.literal: Ning and Vice Commander Zha Dashou led three thousand picked troops lying in ambush on the eastern-river bypath, and again cut off more than three hundred sixty heads.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ning and Vice Commander Zha Dashou, with three thousand elite troops in ambush on a river path, cut down another three hundred sixty heads.

sentences.zh: 乘勝逐北。

translations.literal: Riding victory they pursued north.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed the pursuit in triumph.

sentences.zh: 十九日，如柏遂復開城。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day Rubai thereupon recovered Kaesong.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth Rubai recovered Kaesong.

sentences.zh: 所失黃海、平安、京畿、江源四道並復。

translations.literal: The four circuits lost—Hwanghae, Pyeongan, Gyeonggi, and Gangwon—were all together recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The four lost provinces—Hwanghae, Pyeongan, Gyeonggi, and Gangwon—were all restored.

sentences.zh: 酋清正據鹹鏡，亦遁還王京。

translations.literal: Chieftain-commander Kato Kiyomasa was still holding Hamgyeong, and he too fled back to the royal capital.
translations.idiomatic: Kato Kiyomasa, who still held Hamgyeong, also fled back to Seoul.

sentences.zh: 官軍既連勝，有輕敵心。

translations.literal: The government troops, having won in succession, had a heart of underestimating the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: After successive victories the Ming army grew overconfident.

sentences.zh: 二十七日再進師。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh day they advanced the army again.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh they marched again.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮人以賊棄王京告。

translations.literal: Koreans reported that the bandits had abandoned the royal capital.
translations.idiomatic: Korean informants reported that the Japanese had abandoned the capital.

sentences.zh: 如松信之，將輕騎趨碧蹄館。

translations.literal: Rusong believed it and, leading light cavalry, hastened toward Byeokje Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong believed them and rode ahead with a light cavalry force toward Byeokjegwan.

sentences.zh: 距王京三十里，猝遇倭，圍數重。

translations.literal: Thirty li from the royal capital, they suddenly encountered Japanese and were surrounded in many rings.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li from Seoul they suddenly ran into Japanese forces and were encircled on every side.

sentences.zh: 如松督部下鏖戰。

translations.literal: Rusong supervised his subordinates in fierce battle.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong fought at the head of his men in a desperate engagement.

sentences.zh: 一金甲倭搏如松急，指揮李有聲殊死救，被殺。

translations.literal: A gold-armored Japanese pressed Rusong urgently in combat; Commander Li Yousheng rescued him at the cost of his life and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: A Japanese warrior in golden armor closed on Rusong; Commander Li Yousheng threw himself into the melee to save him and was killed.

sentences.zh: 如柏、寧等奮前夾擊，如梅射金甲倭墜馬，楊元兵亦至，斫重圍入，倭乃退，官軍喪失甚多。

translations.literal: Rubai, Ning, and others fought forward in pincer attack; Rumei shot the gold-armored Japanese off his horse; Yang Yuan's troops also arrived, hacking through the heavy encirclement to enter, and the Japanese then retreated, while the government army lost many.
translations.idiomatic: Rubai and Li Ning struck from the flanks, Rumei shot down the golden-armored warrior, and Yang Yuan's troops hacked their way in—forcing the Japanese to withdraw at the cost of heavy Ming casualties.

sentences.zh: 會天久雨，騎入稻畦中不得逞。

translations.literal: It happened that heaven rained long; cavalry entering rice paddies could not show their prowess.
translations.idiomatic: Prolonged rains turned the paddies to mud and left the cavalry helpless.

sentences.zh: 倭背嶽山，面漢水，聯營城中，廣樹飛樓，箭砲不絕，官軍乃退駐開城。

translations.literal: The Japanese backed on Mount Naksan, faced the Han River, joined camps in the city, widely raised flying towers, arrows and cannon unceasing, and the government army thereupon withdrew to garrison Kaesong.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese entrenched on Namsan above the Han, linked camps throughout the city, and rained arrows and cannon fire from siege towers until the Ming army pulled back to Kaesong.

sentences.zh: 二月既望，諜報倭以二十萬眾入寇。

translations.literal: On the full moon of the second month, spies reported the Japanese invading with two hundred thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the mid-month full moon, intelligence claimed two hundred thousand Japanese were on the move.

sentences.zh: 如松令元軍平壤，扼大同江，接餉道；

translations.literal: Rusong ordered Yuan to station troops at Pyongyang, choke the Taedong River, and connect the supply route;
translations.idiomatic: Rusong posted Yang Yuan at Pyongyang to hold the Taedong and keep the supply line open;

sentences.zh: 如柏等軍寶山諸處為聲援；

translations.literal: Rubai and others stationed armies at Mount Bao and various places as sounding support;
translations.idiomatic: Rubai took up positions around Mount Bao to support the main force;

sentences.zh: 大受軍臨津；

translations.literal: Dashou's army was at the Imjin.
translations.idiomatic: Zha Dashou held the Imjin line;

sentences.zh: 留寧、承訓軍開城；

translations.literal: he left Ning and Chengxun's armies at Kaesong;
translations.idiomatic: Li Ning and Zu Chengxun remained at Kaesong;

sentences.zh: 而身自東西調度。

translations.literal: while he personally from east and west deployed and directed.
translations.idiomatic: while he personally shuttled between the wings to direct operations.

sentences.zh: 聞倭將平秀嘉據龍山倉，積粟數十萬，密令大受率死士從間焚之。

translations.literal: Hearing the Japanese general Hiraka Shuka held Ryongsan granary with grain accumulated in hundreds of thousands, he secretly ordered Dashou to lead death-daring warriors by a bypath to burn it.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that a Japanese commander held the Ryongsan granaries with hundreds of thousands of bushels of rice, he sent Zha Dashou with picked men on a secret raid to burn them.

sentences.zh: 倭遂乏食。

translations.literal: The Japanese thereupon lacked food.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese soon ran short of provisions.

sentences.zh: 初，官軍捷平壤，鋒銳甚，不復問封貢事。

translations.literal: At first the government army was victorious at Pyongyang; their edge was very sharp, and they no longer inquired into enfeoffment-tribute affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory at Pyongyang the Ming army was at its sharpest and gave no further thought to negotiated peace.

sentences.zh: 及碧蹄敗衄，如鬆氣大索，應昌、如松急欲休息，而倭亦芻糧並絕，且懲平壤之敗，有歸志，於是惟敬款議復行。

translations.literal: When Byeokje defeat set in, Rusong's spirit greatly contracted, Yingchang and Rusong urgently wished to rest, while the Japanese too had fodder and grain both cut off and, moreover, mindful of the Pyongyang defeat, had a will to return, and thus Shen Weijing's cordial talks again proceeded.
translations.idiomatic: After the rout at Byeokjegwan Rusong's confidence collapsed; he and Song Yingchang were eager to regroup, while the Japanese—short of supplies and chastened by Pyongyang—were ready to withdraw, and Shen Weijing's peace negotiations resumed.

sentences.zh: 四月十八日，倭棄王京遁，如松與應昌入城，遣兵渡漢江尾倭後，將擊其惰歸。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day of the fourth month the Japanese abandoned the royal capital and fled; Rusong and Yingchang entered the city, sent troops across the Han River to tail the Japanese rear, and were about to strike their relaxed return.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth of the fourth month the Japanese quit Seoul; Rusong and Song Yingchang entered the city and sent troops across the Han to harass the retreating enemy.

sentences.zh: 倭步步為營，分番迭休，官軍不敢擊。

translations.literal: The Japanese at every step made camps, divided shifts in rotation to rest, and the government army did not dare strike.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese retreated in fortified stages, resting in relays, and the Ming army dared not attack.

sentences.zh: 倭乃結營釜山，為久留計。

translations.literal: The Japanese thereupon established camps at Busan for a long-stay plan.
translations.idiomatic: They fortified Busan, plainly intending to remain.

sentences.zh: 時兵部尚書石星力主封貢，議撤兵，獨留劉綎拒守。

translations.literal: At the time Minister of War Shi Xing forcefully advocated enfeoffment-tribute, discussing withdrawing troops and leaving only Liu Ting to resist and hold.
translations.idiomatic: War Minister Shi Xing pushed hard for a tributary settlement, arguing for withdrawal and leaving only Liu Ting to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 如松乃以十二月班師。

translations.literal: Rusong thereupon in the twelfth month returned the army to barracks.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong withdrew his army in the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 論功，加太子太保，增歲祿百石。

translations.literal: Discussing merit, he was advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with yearly salary grain increased by one hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted an extra hundred piculs of annual grain.

sentences.zh: 言者詆其和親辱國，屢攻擊之。

translations.literal: Memorialists slandered his marriage-alliance as shaming the state and repeatedly attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Critics denounced the peace as a national humiliation and attacked him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 帝不問。

translations.literal: The emperor did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid them no heed.

sentences.zh: 二十五年冬，遼東總兵董一元罷，廷推者三，中旨特用如松。

translations.literal: In winter of the twenty-fifth year Liaodong regional commander Dong Yiyuan was dismissed; three were pushed by the court, but an imperial rescript specially employed Rusong.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year twenty-five Dong Yiyuan was removed as Liaodong commander; though three candidates were nominated, the throne appointed Rusong by special edict.

sentences.zh: 言路復交章力爭，帝置不報。

translations.literal: The censorate route again submitted memorials in succession forcefully contending, and the emperor set them aside without reply.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate protested again in a flood of memorials, but the emperor ignored them.

sentences.zh: 如松感帝知，氣益奮。

translations.literal: Rusong, moved by the emperor's knowing him, was ever more spirited.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for the emperor's trust, Rusong fought with redoubled zeal.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，土蠻寇犯遼東。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the next year Tuman the bandit invaded and violated Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: The following April the Tümen Mongols raided Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 如松率輕騎遠出搗巢，中伏力戰死。

translations.literal: Rusong led light cavalry far out to strike nests, hit an ambush, fought fiercely, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong led a light cavalry force on a deep raid, walked into an ambush, and died fighting.

sentences.zh: 帝痛悼，令具衣冠歸葬，贈少保、甯遠伯，立祠，諡忠烈。

translations.literal: The emperor grieved in pain, ordered complete cap and robes for burial back home, posthumously bestowed Junior Guardian and Baron of Ningyuan, established a shrine, and gave the posthumous title Loyal and Fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply mourning him, the emperor ordered him buried in full regalia, posthumously made him Junior Guardian and Baron of Ningyuan, raised a shrine, and gave him the posthumous name Zhonglie ("Loyal and Valiant").

sentences.zh: 以其弟如梅代為總兵官，授長子世忠錦衣衛指揮使，掌南鎮撫司，仍充甯遠伯勳衛，復廕一子本衛指揮使，世襲。

translations.literal: With his younger brother Rumei replacing him as regional commander-in-chief, he invested eldest son Shizhong as Embroidered-Uniform Guard commander, in charge of the Southern Pacification Office, still serving as Ningyuan baron hereditary guard, and again enfeoffed one son as this guard's commander with hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Li Rumei succeeded him as commander; his eldest son Shizhong was made an Embroidered-Uniform Guard commander and placed in the Southern Pacification Office, retaining the Ningyuan baron's hereditary guard, and another son was enfeoffed with a hereditary command in the same guard.

sentences.zh: 恤典優渥，皆出特恩雲。

translations.literal: Mourning rites were generous and ample, all coming from special grace, as the saying goes.
translations.idiomatic: The mourning honors were extraordinarily generous, all by special imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 世忠未久卒，無子。

translations.literal: Shizhong died not long after, without a son.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong died soon afterward without an heir.

sentences.zh: 弟顯忠由廕曆遼東副總兵，當嗣爵，朝臣方惡李氏，無為言者。

translations.literal: Younger brother Xianzhong by enfeoffment rose through Liaodong deputy regional commander and ought to inherit the title, but court ministers just then hated the Li clan and there was none to speak for him.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xianzhong, who had risen to deputy commander of Liaodong through enfeoffment, should have inherited the title, but the court despised the Li family and no one spoke on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 至崇禎中，如松妻武氏訴於朝。

translations.literal: By the Chongzhen reign Rusong's wife Lady Wu appealed at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongzhen era Rusong's widow Lady Wu petitioned the throne.

sentences.zh: 章下部議，竟寢。

translations.literal: The memorial went down to ministries for discussion and in the end was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the ministries, but the matter died in committee.

sentences.zh: 後莊烈帝念成梁功，顯忠子尊祖得嗣甯遠伯。

translations.literal: Later the Zhuanglie Emperor, mindful of Chengliang's merit, allowed Xianzhong's son Zunzu to inherit Baron of Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Chongzhen Emperor, remembering Li Chengliang's service, allowed Xianzhong's son Zunzu to succeed as Baron of Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 闖賊陷京師，遇難。

translations.literal: When the roving-bandit armies seized the capital, he met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He perished when Li Zicheng's rebels took Beijing.

sentences.zh: 子 如柏

translations.literal: Son: Rubai
translations.idiomatic: His son: Li Rubai

sentences.zh: 如柏，字子貞，成梁第二子。

translations.literal: Rubai, styled Zizhen, was Chengliang's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rubai, courtesy name Zizhen, was Li Chengliang's second son.

sentences.zh: 由父廕為錦衣千戶。

translations.literal: Through his father's enfeoffment he became Embroidered-Uniform Guard chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service through his father's privilege as a chiliarch in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 嘗與客會飲，砲聲徹大內，下吏免官。

translations.literal: Once feasting with guests in drinking assembly, cannon sound penetrated the great inner court, and the investigating officials dismissed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet with guests his fireworks thundered into the Forbidden City; the authorities stripped him of rank.

sentences.zh: 再以廕為指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Again through enfeoffment he became assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: He later regained office through enfeoffment as assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 數從父出塞有功，曆密雲遊擊，黃花嶺參將，薊鎮副總兵。

translations.literal: Several times following his father beyond the pass he had merit, passing through Miyun mobile-corps commander, Yellow Flower Ridge brigade commander, and Jizhou garrison deputy regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned beyond the passes with his father, later serving as mobile corps commander at Miyun, brigade commander at Yellow Flower Ridge, and deputy commander at Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十六年，御史任養心言：「李氏兵權太盛。

translations.literal: In the Wanli sixteenth year Censor Ren Yangxin said: "The Li clan's military authority is too great.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Wanli Censor Ren Yangxin memorialized: "The Li family's military power has grown excessive.

sentences.zh: 姻親廝養分操兵柄，環神京數千里，縱橫蟠據，不可動搖。

translations.literal: Affinal kin and house-bred servants each grasped military authority, encircling the divine capital for several thousand li, sprawling and coiled—impossible to shake.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives and household clients command troops across thousands of li around the capital in a network no one can challenge.

sentences.zh: 如柏貪淫，跋扈尤甚。

translations.literal: Rubai was greedy and licentious, overbearing especially.
translations.idiomatic: Rubai's greed and arrogance were worst of all.

sentences.zh: 不早為計，恐生他變。」

translations.literal: If one does not plan early, I fear other changes will arise."
translations.idiomatic: Unless something is done soon, I fear worse trouble will follow.

sentences.zh: 帝乃解如伯任。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon relieved Rubo's post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then removed Rubai from office.

sentences.zh: 於是成梁上書乞罷，並請盡罷子弟官，帝慰留不許。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chengliang submitted a memorial begging dismissal and asked to dismiss all sons and brothers from office; the emperor comforted and retained him, not permitting.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengliang then asked to resign and to strip all his sons of their posts; the emperor refused and kept him in service.

sentences.zh: 久之，起故官，署宣府參將。

translations.literal: After long time he was raised to his old office, acting as Xuanfu brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he was reinstated as acting brigade commander at Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 引疾歸。

translations.literal: He cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 如松之禦倭朝鮮也，詔如柏署都督僉事，先率師赴援。

translations.literal: When Rusong was defending against Japanese in Korea, an edict ordered Rubai to act as regional vice commander-in-chief and first lead troops to go aid.
translations.idiomatic: When Rusong was sent to Korea, Rubai was named acting regional vice commander and ordered ahead with the relief force.

sentences.zh: 既拔平壤，如柏疾趨開城，攻克之，斬首百六十有奇。

translations.literal: Once Pyongyang was taken, Rubai swiftly hastened to Kaesong, captured it, and beheaded more than one hundred sixty.
translations.idiomatic: After Pyongyang fell he rushed on Kaesong, took it, and counted more than one hundred sixty heads.

sentences.zh: 師旋，進都督同知，為五軍營副將。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was advanced to regional commander in chief and made Five-Camps deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was promoted to regional commander in chief and made deputy general of the Five Camps.

sentences.zh: 尋出為貴州總兵官。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Guizhou regional commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted as commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，改鎮寧夏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year his garrison was changed to Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-three he was transferred to command Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 著力兔犯平虜、橫城，如伯邀之，大獲，斬首二百七十有奇。

translations.literal: Zhali Tu violated Pinglu and Hengcheng; Rubo intercepted him with great gain and beheaded more than two hundred seventy.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhali Tu raided Pinglu and Hengcheng, Rubai ambushed him for a major victory, taking more than two hundred seventy heads.

sentences.zh: 進右都督。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Right Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 再以疾歸，家居二十餘年。

translations.literal: Again citing illness he returned, dwelling at home more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Illness sent him home again, where he lived in retirement for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 會遼東總兵官張承廕戰歿，文武大臣英國公張惟賢等合疏薦如柏，詔以故官鎮遼東。

translations.literal: It happened that Liaodong regional commander-in-chief Zhang Chengyin died in battle; civil and military great ministers including Duke of England Zhang Weixian jointly memorialized recommending Rubai, and an edict ordered his former office to garrison Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Chengyin was killed in action, Zhang Weixian and other ministers jointly recommended Rubai, and the throne restored him to command Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 蒙古炒花入犯，督諸將擊卻之。

translations.literal: The Mongol Chahua entered in violation; he supervised various generals to strike and repel them.
translations.idiomatic: He led his officers to repulse an invasion by the Mongol leader Chahua.

sentences.zh: 始成梁、如松為將，厚畜健兒，故所向克捷。

translations.literal: At the beginning when Chengliang and Rusong were generals, they thickly stored stout youths, hence wherever they went they overcame and were sharp.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengliang and Rusong commanded, they kept large corps of hardened warriors and rarely lost a battle.

sentences.zh: 至是，父兄故部曲已無復存，而如柏暨諸弟放情酒色，亦無復少年英銳。

translations.literal: By this time the father's and brothers' old retainers no longer existed, while Rubai together with various younger brothers indulged wine and women and likewise no longer had the sharpness of youth.
translations.idiomatic: By then their father's veterans were gone, and Rubai and his brothers had squandered their youth in drink and women.

sentences.zh: 特以李氏世將，起自廢籍中。

translations.literal: Only because the Li clan were hereditary generals were they raised from discharged registers.
translations.idiomatic: They were restored only because the Lis were hereditary frontier commanders.

sentences.zh: 顧如柏中情怯，惟左次避敵而已。

translations.literal: Yet Rubai's inner disposition was timid; he only took inferior position to avoid the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Rubai was timid at heart and would only take second rank to keep clear of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 我大清師臨河，如柏故引軍防懿路。

translations.literal: Our Great Qing army approached the river; Rubai purposely drew troops to defend Yilu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing army reached the river, Rubai kept his forces on the defensive at Yilu.

sentences.zh: 及楊鎬四路出師，令如柏以一軍出鴉鶻關。

translations.literal: When Yang Hao sent four routes out as army, he ordered Rubai with one army to exit through Yahu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In Yang Hao's four-pronged campaign Rubai was assigned one column through Yahu Pass.

sentences.zh: 甫抵虎攔路，鎬聞杜松、馬林兩軍已覆，急檄如柏還。

translations.literal: Just as they reached Tiger-blocking Road, Hao heard Du Song and Ma Lin's two armies had already been destroyed and urgently dispatched orders for Rubai to return.
translations.idiomatic: Rubai had barely reached Hulun when Yang Hao, learning that Du Song and Ma Lin had been destroyed, ordered him back.

sentences.zh: 大清哨兵二十人見之，登山鳴螺，作大軍追擊狀，如柏軍大驚，奔走相蹴死者千余人。

translations.literal: Our Great Qing's twenty sentry soldiers saw them, climbed the mountain and sounded conchs, making the appearance of a great army pursuing, and Rubai's army was greatly alarmed; fleeing and trampling one another, more than a thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty Qing scouts sighted them, climbed a hill, and blew horns as if a great host were pursuing; Rubai's panicked troops trampled one another to death—more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 御史給事中交章論劾，給事中李奇珍連疏爭尤力。

translations.literal: Investigating censors and supervising secretaries submitted memorials in succession impeaching; Supervising Secretary Li Qizhen in linked memorials contended especially forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Censors and supervising secretaries denounced him in a storm of memorials; Li Qizhen led the charge with repeated petitions.

sentences.zh: 帝終念李氏，詔還候勘。

translations.literal: The emperor in the end remembered the Li clan and ordered him back to await investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, still mindful of the Li family's service, recalled Rubai pending inquiry.

sentences.zh: 既入都，言者不已。

translations.literal: Once he entered the capital, memorialists did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached Beijing the attacks did not stop.

sentences.zh: 如柏懼，遂自裁。

translations.literal: Rubai feared and thereupon cut his own life.
translations.idiomatic: In fear Rubai took his own life.

sentences.zh: 子 如楨

translations.literal: Son: Ruzhen
translations.idiomatic: His son: Li Ruzhen

sentences.zh: 如楨，成梁第三子。

translations.literal: Ruzhen was Chengliang's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruzhen was Li Chengliang's third son.

sentences.zh: 由父廕為指揮使。

translations.literal: Through father's enfeoffment he became commander.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service through his father's privilege as a guard commander.

sentences.zh: 屢加至右都督，並在錦衣。

translations.literal: Repeatedly advanced to Right Regional Commander, concurrently in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Regional Commander while remaining in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 嘗掌南、北鎮撫司，提督西司房，列環衛者四十年。

translations.literal: He once managed south and north Pacification Offices, supervised the Western Bureau room, and stood in the encircling guard for forty years.
translations.idiomatic: He headed both the southern and northern Pacification Offices, supervised the Western Bureau, and served in the capital guard for forty years.

sentences.zh: 最後，軍政拾遺，部議罷職，章久留不下。

translations.literal: Finally, on military administration pick-up of omissions, the ministry discussed dismissing him from office, yet the memorial long remained without issuance.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end a personnel review found grounds to remove him, but the memorial sat unreleased for a long time.

sentences.zh: 如楨雖將家子，然未曆行陣，不知兵。

translations.literal: Although Ruzhen was a general's household son, he had yet to pass through battle formations and did not know military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Though born to a military family, Ruzhen had never seen combat and knew nothing of war.

sentences.zh: 及兄如柏革任，遼人謂李氏世鎮遼東，邊人憚服，非再用李氏不可，巡撫周永春以為言。

translations.literal: When elder brother Rubai was removed from post, Liaodong people said the Li clan for generations garrisoned Liaodong and border people feared and submitted—without reusing the Li clan it could not be done—and Grand Coordinator Zhou Yongchun spoke accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: After Rubai was dismissed, Liaodong argued that only a Li could hold the frontier's respect; Grand Coordinator Zhou Yongchun said as much to the court.

sentences.zh: 而是時如柏兄弟獨如楨在，兵部尚書黃嘉善遂徇其請，以如楨名上，帝即可之。

translations.literal: Yet at this time among Rubai's brothers only Ruzhen remained; War Minister Huang Jiashan thereupon followed their request, putting up Ruzhen's name, and the emperor promptly approved.
translations.idiomatic: With Rubai gone, Huang Jiashan gave in to the plea and nominated Ruzhen; the emperor approved at once.

sentences.zh: 時萬曆四十七年四月也。

translations.literal: It was the fourth month of Wanli forty-seventh year.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the fourth month of the forty-seventh year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 如楨藉父兄勢，又自以錦衣近臣，不肯居人下。

translations.literal: Ruzhen relied on father and brothers' power and moreover regarded himself as an Embroidered-Uniform intimate minister, unwilling to place himself below others.
translations.idiomatic: Trading on his family's influence and his position as a palace guards officer, Ruzhen refused to take orders from anyone.

sentences.zh: 未出關，即遣使與總督汪可受講鈞禮，朝議譁然，嘉善亦特疏言之。

translations.literal: Before exiting the pass he sent envoys with Governor-General Wang Keshou to discuss equal-bracket rites; court discussion was in uproar, and Jiashan also submitted a special memorial on it.
translations.idiomatic: Before even leaving the capital he sent envoys to demand ceremonial parity with Governor-General Wang Keshou; the court was outraged, and Huang Jiashan filed a special protest.

sentences.zh: 如楨始怏怏去。

translations.literal: Ruzhen only then departed in displeasure.
translations.idiomatic: Ruzhen set out in sullen resentment.

sentences.zh: 既抵遼，經略楊鎬使守鐵嶺。

translations.literal: Once he reached Liaodong, Commissioner-in-chief Yang Hao had him guard Tieling.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Liaodong Yang Hao stationed him at Tieling.

sentences.zh: 鐵嶺故李氏宗族墳墓所在。

translations.literal: Tieling was where the Li clan's ancestral graves lay of old.
translations.idiomatic: Tieling was the ancestral seat of the Li clan.

sentences.zh: 當如柏還京，其族党部曲高貲者悉隨之而西，城中為空。

translations.literal: When Rubai returned to the capital, his clan partisans and retainers of high wealth all followed west with him, and the city became empty.
translations.idiomatic: When Rubai left for Beijing his wealthy kinsmen and clients went with him, and Tieling was left hollow.

sentences.zh: 後鎬以孤城難守，令如楨還屯瀋陽，僅以參將丁碧等防守，力益弱。

translations.literal: Later Hao, because the lonely city was hard to defend, ordered Ruzhen back to garrison Shenyang, leaving only Brigade Commander Ding Bi and others to defend—the strength ever weaker.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hao later judged the city indefensible and moved Ruzhen to Shenyang, leaving only Ding Bi's brigade to hold Tieling—further weakening the garrison.

sentences.zh: 大清兵臨城，如楨擁兵不救，城遂失。

translations.literal: Our Great Qing troops reached the city; Ruzhen hugged troops and did not rescue, and the city thereupon fell.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing army came to Tieling, Ruzhen refused to move to its relief and the city was lost.

sentences.zh: 言官交章論列，經略熊廷弼亦論如楨十不堪，乃罷任。

translations.literal: Memorialist officials submitted memorials in succession discussing and arranging; Commissioner-in-chief Xiong Tingbi also discussed Ruzhen's ten counts of unfitness, and then he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Censors denounced him in droves; Xiong Tingbi listed ten reasons he was unfit for command, and he was removed.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，言者復力攻，下獄論死。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, memorialists again attacked forcefully; he was put in prison and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign critics renewed their attack; he was imprisoned and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年，帝念成梁勳，特免死充軍。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen fourth year the emperor, mindful of Chengliang's merit, specially exempted death and made military exile.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongzhen the emperor, remembering Li Chengliang's service, spared his life and sentenced him to military exile.

sentences.zh: 子 如樟

translations.literal: Son: Ruzhang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Li Ruzhang.

sentences.zh: 如樟，亦由父廕，曆都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Ruzhang also received office through his father's yin privilege and rose through the ranks to Assistant Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruzhang likewise entered service through his father's hereditary privilege and eventually became an assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 從兄如松征寧夏，先登有功，累進都督僉事。

translations.literal: When his cousin Rusong campaigned in Ningxia he was first to scale the walls and was credited with merit, and through repeated advancement rose to Regional Vice Commander.
translations.idiomatic: On his cousin Rusong's Ningxia campaign he led the first assault over the walls and was rewarded; he was promoted repeatedly until he became a regional vice commander.

sentences.zh: 曆廣西、延綏總兵官。

translations.literal: He successively served as Regional Commander in Guangxi and Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: He held regional commands in Guangxi and then in Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 子 如梅

translations.literal: Son: Rumei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Li Rumei.

sentences.zh: 如梅，字子清。

translations.literal: Rumei, style name Ziqing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rumei, whose style name was Ziqing.

sentences.zh: 亦由父廕，曆都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: He too received office through his father's yin privilege and rose through the ranks to Assistant Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise entered service through his father's hereditary privilege and eventually became an assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 從兄如松征日本，卻敵先登。

translations.literal: When his cousin Rusong campaigned in Japan he repelled the enemy and was first to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: On Rusong's campaign against Japan he repulsed the enemy and was first over the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 屢遷遼東副總兵。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred and made Liaodong Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly until he became vice regional commander of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，炒花、卜言兔將入犯，如梅謀先襲之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Chaohua and Buyantu were about to invade; Rumei planned to strike them first.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-four Chaohua and Buyantu were preparing a raid; Li Rumei proposed a preemptive strike.

sentences.zh: 督部將方時新等出塞三百里，直搗其廬帳，斬首百餘級而還。

translations.literal: He supervised subordinate officers Fang Shixin and others, who went three hundred li beyond the border, struck straight at their yurt encampment, took more than one hundred heads, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He led Fang Shixin and other officers three hundred li beyond the border in a direct attack on their camp, took over a hundred heads, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年，如梅與參政楊鎬謀復從鎮西堡出塞，潛襲敵營，失利，損部將十人，士卒百六十人。

translations.literal: The next year Rumei with Participant Yang Hao again schemed to go beyond the border from Zhenxi Fort and secretly raid the enemy camp; they met defeat, losing ten staff officers and one hundred sixty soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Rumei and Civil Participant Yang Hao planned another sortie from Zhenxi Fort to surprise the enemy camp; the attack failed, costing ten officers and a hundred and sixty men.

sentences.zh: 如梅以血戰重創，免罪。

translations.literal: Rumei for bloody fighting received grave wounds and was exempted from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Rumei had been badly wounded in fierce fighting and was spared punishment.

sentences.zh: 日本封事敗，其年八月，進署都督僉事，充禦倭副總兵，赴朝鮮援剿，時麻貴三路進師，令如梅將左軍，與右軍共攻蔚山。

translations.literal: The Japanese investiture affair failed; in the eighth month of that year he was advanced to acting Regional Vice Commander and appointed Vice Regional Commander for defense against the Wo, sent to Korea to aid in suppression; at that time Ma Gui was advancing in three columns and ordered Rumei to command the left army, which together with the right army jointly attacked Ulsan.
translations.idiomatic: After the failed Japanese investiture negotiations, in the eighth month of that year he was made acting regional vice commander and deputy general for defense against Japan, and sent to Korea. Ma Gui was advancing in three columns and assigned Rumei the left wing to attack Ulsan together with the right.

sentences.zh: 如梅偕參將楊登山騎兵先進，設伏海濱，而令遊擊擺賽以輕騎誘賊，斬首四百有奇，餘賊遁歸島山。

translations.literal: Rumei with Assistant Commander Yang Dengshan's cavalry advanced first, set ambushes along the seashore, and ordered Mobile Corps Commander Bai Sai with light cavalry to lure the enemy; they took more than four hundred heads, and the remnant enemy fled back to Waesan.
translations.idiomatic: Rumei advanced first with Yang Dengshan's cavalry, laid ambushes along the coast, and sent Bai Sai with a light detachment to bait the Japanese—over four hundred were killed, and the survivors retreated to Waesan.

sentences.zh: 副將陳寅冒矢石奮呼上，破柵兩重。

translations.literal: Vice Commander Chen Yin braved arrows and stones, shouting as he charged up, and broke through two palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commander Chen Yin charged under fire, shouting encouragement, and broke through two lines of palisades.

sentences.zh: 至第三柵，垂拔，楊鎬為總理，宿與如梅昵，不欲寅功出其上，遽鳴金收軍。

translations.literal: Reaching the third palisade, about to be taken, Yang Hao as supreme coordinator had long been intimate with Rumei and did not want Chen Yin's merit to surpass him; he abruptly sounded the gong to recall the army.
translations.idiomatic: At the third palisade, on the verge of capture, supreme coordinator Yang Hao—long friendly with Rumei and unwilling to see Chen Yin win greater glory—suddenly ordered a withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 翊日，如梅至，攻之，不能拔。

translations.literal: The next day Rumei arrived, attacked it, and could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Rumei took command and assaulted the position, but could not capture it.

sentences.zh: 已而賊援至，如梅軍先奔，諸軍亦相繼潰。

translations.literal: Before long enemy reinforcements arrived; Rumei's army fled first, and the various armies also collapsed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Japanese reinforcements soon arrived; Rumei's troops broke first, and the rest of the army followed in rout.

sentences.zh: 贊畫主事丁應泰劾鎬，並劾如梅當斬者二，當罪者十，帝不納。

translations.literal: Planning secretary Ding Yingtai impeached Hao and also impeached Rumei with two capital offenses and ten punishable offenses; the emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Planning secretary Ding Yingtai impeached Yang Hao and charged Rumei with two capital crimes and ten lesser offenses, but the emperor took no action.

sentences.zh: 旋用為禦倭總兵官。

translations.literal: He was soon employed as Regional Commander for defense against the Wo.
translations.idiomatic: Rumei was soon appointed regional commander for defense against Japan.

sentences.zh: 會其兄如松戰歿，即命如梅馳代之。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Rusong died in battle, he was immediately ordered to ride post-haste and replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When his brother Rusong fell in battle, Rumei was ordered to hurry north and succeed him.

sentences.zh: 逾年，坐擁兵畏敵，劾罷。

translations.literal: After a year, for holding troops and fearing the enemy, he was impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he was impeached for hoarding troops and shying from the enemy and was removed from command.

sentences.zh: 久之，起僉書左府。

translations.literal: After a long time he was raised to serve as secretary in the left bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was restored to a secretarial post in the left military commission.

sentences.zh: 四十年，鎬巡撫遼東，力薦如梅為帥。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year Hao was grand coordinator of Liaodong and strenuously recommended Rumei as commander.
translations.idiomatic: In year forty, as grand coordinator of Liaodong, Yang Hao pressed hard for Rumei to be made supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 不得，至以死爭。

translations.literal: He did not obtain it, going so far as to contend with his life.
translations.idiomatic: When he failed, he went so far as to threaten his own life over the appointment.

sentences.zh: 給事中麻僖、御史楊州鶴力持不可，乃止。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Ma Xi and Censor Yang Zhouhe firmly held that it could not be done, and so it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Ma Xi and Censor Yang Zhouhe objected firmly, and the appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 成梁諸子，如松最果敢，有父風。

translations.literal: Among Chengliang's sons Rusong was boldest and most resolute, with his father's bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Of Li Chengliang's sons, Rusong was the boldest and most resolute—very much in his father's mold.

sentences.zh: 其次稱如梅，然躁動，非大將才，獨楊鎬深信。

translations.literal: Next in reputation was Rumei, yet he was restless and impetuous—not talent for a great commander; only Yang Hao deeply trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Rumei ranked next, but he was impulsive and restless, lacking the temperament of a great commander; only Yang Hao placed full faith in him.

sentences.zh: 後復倚任其兄如柏，卒以致敗。

translations.literal: Later he again relied on and entrusted his elder brother Rubai, and in the end thereby met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hao later leaned on his brother Rubai as well—and that dependence ultimately led to disaster.

sentences.zh: 麻貴，大同右衛人。

translations.literal: Ma Gui was a man of Datong Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui was a native of Datong Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 父祿，嘉靖中為大同參將，從鎮帥劉漢襲板升，大獲。

translations.literal: His father Lu in the Jiajing reign served as Datong Assistant Commander; following the garrison commander Liu Han he raided Bansheng and gained greatly.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ma Lu had been a Datong assistant commander under Jiajing; he followed Regional Commander Liu Han on a raid against Bansheng and won a major victory.

sentences.zh: 俺答圍右衛，祿與副將尚表固守，乘間擊斬其部長，寇乃引退。

translations.literal: Altan besieged Right Guard; Lu with Vice Commander Shang Biao held firm, seized an interval to strike and behead a tribal leader, and the raiders then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Altan besieged Right Guard, Ma Lu and Vice Commander Shang Biao held the walls; catching an opening, they killed a tribal chief and drove the raiders off.

sentences.zh: 辛愛犯京東，祿以宣府副總兵入衛，與子遊擊錦並有卻敵功。

translations.literal: Xin'ai invaded eastern Beijing; Lu as Xuanfu Vice Regional Commander entered to guard the capital, and together with his son Mobile Corps Commander Jin both had merit in repelling the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin'ai threatened the eastern capital, Ma Lu marched east as Xuanfu vice commander; he and his son Jin both distinguished themselves in repelling the invasion.

sentences.zh: 貴由舍人從軍，積功至都指揮僉事，充宣府遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: Gui from personal attendant followed the army, accumulated merit to Assistant Regional Commander, and served as Xuanfu Mobile Corps Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui entered service as a garrison attendant, rose through merit to assistant regional commander, and was appointed mobile corps commander of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中，遷大同新平堡參將。

translations.literal: In the Longqing reign he was transferred to Datong Xinping Fort Assistant Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Under Longqing he became assistant commander at Xinping Fort, Datong.

sentences.zh: 寇大入，掠山陰、懷仁、應州。

translations.literal: The raiders entered on a large scale, plundering Shanyin, Huairen, and Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders poured in, pillaging Shanyin, Huairen, and Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 將吏並獲罪，獨貴與兄副將錦拒戰有功，受賞。

translations.literal: Officers and officials all received punishment; only Gui and his elder brother Vice Commander Jin for resisting battle had merit and received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Most officers were punished; only Ma Gui and his elder brother Jin were rewarded for holding the line in battle.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初，再遷大同副總兵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli he was again transferred to Datong Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wanli he was promoted again to vice regional commander of Datong.

sentences.zh: 十年冬，以都督僉事充寧夏總兵官。

translations.literal: In the winter of the tenth year, with the rank of Regional Vice Commander he served as Ningxia Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year ten he became regional commander of Ningxia with the rank of regional vice commander.

sentences.zh: 無何，徙鎮大同。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to command Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was reassigned to command Datong.

sentences.zh: 時諸部納款久，撦力克襲封順義王，奉中國益虔。

translations.literal: At the time the various tribes had submitted for a long time; Chelik succeeded to enfeoffment as Prince of Shunyi and served the Middle Kingdom all the more devoutly.
translations.idiomatic: The border tribes had been at peace for years; Chelik inherited the Shunyi princedom and professed ever deeper loyalty to the Ming.

sentences.zh: 貴頻以安邊勞蒙賜賚。

translations.literal: Gui frequently for pacifying the border toil received bestowal rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui was repeatedly honored with imperial gifts for keeping the frontier quiet.

sentences.zh: 十九年，為閱視少卿曾乾亨所劾，謫戍邊。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was impeached by Touring Review Junior Minister Zeng Qianheng and banished to garrison the border.
translations.idiomatic: In year nineteen, Junior Minister Zeng Qianheng impeached him, and he was exiled to frontier garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 明年，寧夏哱拜反。

translations.literal: The next year in Ningxia Pai Bai rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Pai Bai rebelled in Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 廷議貴健將知兵，且多畜家丁，乃起戍中為副將，總兵討賊。

translations.literal: The court discussed that Gui was a sturdy general who knew warfare and moreover kept many household troops; he was raised from among the banished garrison troops to Vice Commander and Regional Commander to suppress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The court judged Ma Gui a tough, experienced commander with a large personal following; he was recalled from exile as deputy and supreme commander to crush the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 屢攻城不克。

translations.literal: He repeatedly assaulted the city without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated assaults on the city failed.

sentences.zh: 其五月，哱拜以套寇五百騎圍平虜堡，貴選精卒三百間道馳卻之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Pai Bai with five hundred Ordos horsemen besieged Pinglu Fort; Gui selected three hundred elite soldiers who by hidden path galloped to repulse them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Pai Bai sent five hundred Ordos cavalry to invest Pinglu Fort; Ma Gui picked three hundred elite troops, took a back route, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 俄以總督魏學曾命撫著力兔、銀定、宰僧於橫城，啖以重利，皆不應，貴乃還攻城。

translations.literal: Before long, by Grand Coordinator Wei Xueceng's order he pacified Zhulitu, Yinding, and Zaiseng at Hengcheng, tempting them with heavy profit; all did not respond, and Gui then returned to assault the city.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Wei Xueceng then ordered Ma Gui to win over Zhulitu, Yinding, and Zaiseng at Hengcheng with rich rewards; when they refused, he resumed the siege.

sentences.zh: 寧夏總兵董一奎攻其南，固原總兵李昫攻其西，故總兵劉承嗣攻其北，牛秉忠攻其東，貴以遊兵主策應。

translations.literal: Ningxia Regional Commander Dong Yikui attacked its south, Guyuan Regional Commander Li Xu its west, former Regional Commander Liu Chengsi its north, Niu Bingzhong its east; Gui with mobile troops mainly coordinated responses.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yikui of Ningxia assailed the south, Li Xu of Guyuan the west, the former commander Liu Chengsi the north, and Niu Bingzhong the east, while Ma Gui's mobile detachments coordinated the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 哱拜自北門出戰，將往勾套部，貴逐之入城，別遣將馬孔英、麻承詔等擊套寇援兵，俘斬百二十人。

translations.literal: Pai Bai himself went out to fight from the north gate, about to summon the Ordos tribes; Gui drove him back into the city and separately dispatched officers Ma Kongying, Ma Chengzhao, and others to strike Ordos reinforcement troops, capturing and beheading one hundred twenty men.
translations.idiomatic: Pai Bai sallied from the north gate to summon Ordos allies; Ma Gui drove him back inside and sent Ma Kongying and Ma Chengzhao against the relief column, killing or capturing a hundred and twenty.

sentences.zh: 拜初與套部深相結，諸部長稱之為王。

translations.literal: At first Pai had been deeply allied with the Ordos tribes; the various chieftains called him king.
translations.idiomatic: Pai Bai had once been closely allied with the Ordos chiefs, who addressed him as their king.

sentences.zh: 日坐著力兔帳中，主籌畫，至是不敢復出。

translations.literal: Day after day he sat in Zhulitu's tent directing planning, until he did not dare come out again.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his days in Zhulitu's tent directing strategy—until he no longer dared leave it.

sentences.zh: 俄朝命蕭如薰代董一奎，盡將諸道援兵，以貴為副。

translations.literal: Before long the court ordered Xiao Ruxun to replace Dong Yikui, bringing all relief forces from the various routes, with Gui as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon replaced Dong Yikui with Xiao Ruxun, uniting all relief columns under his command with Ma Gui as his second.

sentences.zh: 而李如松軍亦至，攻益急。

translations.literal: Moreover Li Rusong's army also arrived, and the assault grew all the fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rusong's army arrived as well, and the pressure on the city intensified.

sentences.zh: 賊奉黃金、繡蟒于卜失兔等，請急徇靈州，先據下馬關，沮餉道。

translations.literal: The rebels presented gold and embroidered pythons to Bushitu and others, begging them urgently to strike toward Lingzhou, first seize Xiamaguan Pass, and obstruct the supply route.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent gold and brocade robes to Bushitu and others, urging a rapid thrust toward Lingzhou and seizure of Xiamaguan to cut Ming supply lines.

sentences.zh: 卜失兔與莊禿賴果合兵犯定邊，而宰僧從花馬池西沙湃入。

translations.literal: Bushitu and Zhuang Tülai indeed combined forces to invade Dingbian, while Zaiseng entered from Xishapo west of Huamachi.
translations.idiomatic: Bushitu and Zhuang Tülai joined forces and struck Dingbian, while Zaiseng entered west of Huamachi via Xishapo.

sentences.zh: 貴迎擊，挫宰僧于石溝。

translations.literal: Gui went to meet and attack, routing Zaiseng at Shigou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui intercepted them and defeated Zaiseng at Shigou.

sentences.zh: 會董一元搗土昧巢，諸部長俱解去。

translations.literal: At the same time Dong Yiyuan raided Tumei's nest; the various chieftains all dispersed and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Dong Yiyuan raided the Ordos base at Tumei, and the tribal chiefs withdrew.

sentences.zh: 賊復乞援於著力兔，擁眾大入。

translations.literal: The rebels again begged aid from Zhulitu, and with a gathered host entered on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels appealed again to Zhulitu, who led a large force back into Ming territory.

sentences.zh: 如松率勁騎迎戰張亮堡，自卯迄巳，敵銳甚。

translations.literal: Rusong led crack cavalry to meet battle at Zhangliang Fort; from mao hour to si hour the enemy was very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong met them at Zhangliang Fort with elite cavalry; from dawn through mid-morning the enemy fought fiercely.

sentences.zh: 會貴及李如樟等兵至，夾擊之，寇乃卻。

translations.literal: At that time Gui and Li Ruzhang and others' troops arrived; they pincered and attacked, and the raiders then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Gui and Li Ruzhang arrived with reinforcements, the Ming forces caught the raiders in a pincer and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 逐北至賀蘭山，獲首級百二十餘。

translations.literal: Pursuing north to Helan Mountain, they obtained more than one hundred twenty heads.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit reached Helan Mountain, yielding more than a hundred and twenty heads.

sentences.zh: 持示賊，賊益洶懼。

translations.literal: Displaying them to show the rebels, the rebels grew all the more turbulent in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui displayed the trophies to the besieged garrison, who grew ever more panicked.

sentences.zh: 無何城破，賊盡平。

translations.literal: Before long the city fell and the rebels were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The city soon fell and the rebellion was crushed.

sentences.zh: 貴以功增秩，子予。

translations.literal: Gui for merit had rank increased and his son rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui was promoted for his service and his son received honors.

sentences.zh: 尋擢總兵官，鎮守延綏。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Regional Commander, garrisoning and defending Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made regional commander of Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 二十二年七月，卜失兔糾諸部深入定邊，營張春井。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year seventh month Bushitu rallied the various tribes and deeply penetrated Dingbian, encamping at Zhangchun Well.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year twenty-two Bushitu rallied the tribes for a deep strike into Dingbian and camped at Zhangchun Well.

sentences.zh: 貴乘虛搗其帳於套中，斬首二百五十有奇。

translations.literal: Gui seized the vacuum to raid their tents in the Ordos bend, beheading more than two hundred fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui exploited their absence to strike their camps in the Ordos bend and took more than two hundred fifty heads.

sentences.zh: 還自寧塞，復邀其零騎。

translations.literal: Returning from Ning-sai, he again intercepted their scattered horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: On his return from Ning-sai he ambushed their stragglers.

sentences.zh: 會寇留內地久，轉掠至下馬關。

translations.literal: At that time the raiders had long remained within the border, turning to plunder as far as Xiamaguan.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders had lingered inside the frontier so long that their raids reached Xiamaguan.

sentences.zh: 寧夏總兵蕭如薰不能禦，總督葉夢熊急檄貴赴援。

translations.literal: Ningxia Regional Commander Xiao Ruxun could not repulse them; Grand Coordinator Ye Mengxiong urgently dispatched a call for Gui to go to relieve.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ruxun of Ningxia could not stop them; Grand Coordinator Ye Mengxiong urgently summoned Ma Gui.

sentences.zh: 督副將蕭如蘭等連戰曬馬台、薛家窪，斬首二百三十有奇，獲畜產萬五千。

translations.literal: Supervising Vice Commanders Xiao Rulan and others fought successive battles at Shaima Terrace and Xuejiawa, beheading more than two hundred thirty and obtaining fifteen thousand head of livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui led Xiao Rulan and others in fights at Shaima Terrace and Xuejiawa, killing over two hundred thirty and capturing fifteen thousand animals.

sentences.zh: 帝為告廟宣捷，進署都督同知，予世廕。

translations.literal: The emperor made temple announcement of victory, advanced him to acting Regional Commander-in-Chief, and granted hereditary yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reported victory at the ancestral temple, promoted Ma Gui to acting regional commander-in-chief, and granted him hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 明年，卜失兔復入塞，掠八日而還。

translations.literal: The next year Bushitu again entered the border, plundering eight days then returning.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Bushitu raided the frontier for eight days before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 順義王撦力克約之納款，不從，復擬大入。

translations.literal: Prince of Shunyi Chelik arranged with him to submit; he did not comply and again planned a major entry.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chelik urged him to submit; he refused and prepared another major invasion.

sentences.zh: 貴勒兵萬五千人：遊擊閻逢時等出紅山為中軍，參將師以律等出高家堡、神木、孤山為左軍，參將孫朝梁等出定邊、安邊、平山為右軍，而自以大軍當一面。

translations.literal: Gui mustered fifteen thousand men: Mobile Corps Commander Yan Fengshi and others exited Hongshan as center army; Assistant Commanders Shi Yilü and others exited Gaojiabao, Shenmu, and Gushan as left army; Assistant Commanders Sun Chaoliang and others exited Dingbian, Anbian, and Pingshan as right army; and he himself with the great army faced one direction.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui led fifteen thousand troops—Yan Fengshi's center column through Hongshan, Shi Yilü's left through Gaojiabao, Shenmu, and Gushan, Sun Chaoliang's right through Dingbian, Anbian, and Pingshan, while he took the main force on the decisive front.

sentences.zh: 銜枚疾趨，逾塞六十里。

translations.literal: With gag between teeth they sped, crossing the border sixty li.
translations.idiomatic: They marched in silence sixty li beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 寇莫知所防，大潰。

translations.literal: The raiders did not know what to defend against and collapsed in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Caught off guard, the raiders broke and fled in chaos.

sentences.zh: 俘斬四百有奇，獲馬駝牛羊千五百。

translations.literal: Captured and beheaded more than four hundred; obtained one thousand five hundred horses, camels, cattle, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: They killed or captured over four hundred men and seized some fifteen hundred horses, camels, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 再進秩，予廕。

translations.literal: Rank was again advanced and yin privilege granted.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again and granted hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 尋以病歸。

translations.literal: Soon he returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired due to illness.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，日本封事敗，起貴備倭總兵官，赴朝鮮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the Japanese investiture affair failed; Gui was raised as Regional Commander preparing against the Wo and sent to Korea.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-five, after the failed Japanese investiture talks, Ma Gui was recalled as regional commander for defense against Japan and sent to Korea.

sentences.zh: 已，加提督，盡統南北諸軍。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was made Supreme Commissioner and entirely commanded all northern and southern armies.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named supreme commissioner with authority over all Ming forces in the theater.

sentences.zh: 貴馳至王京，倭已入慶州，據閑山島，圍南原。

translations.literal: Gui galloped to the king's capital; the Wo had already entered Gyeongju, held Hansan Island, and besieged Namwon.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui rushed to Seoul, but the Japanese had already taken Gyeongju, occupied Hansan Island, and were besieging Namwon.

sentences.zh: 守將楊元遁，全州守將陳愚衷亦遁，倭乘勢逼王京。

translations.literal: Garrison commander Yang Yuan fled; Jeonju garrison commander Chen Yuzhong also fled; the Wo seized momentum and pressed on the king's capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuan, the defender of Namwon, fled; Chen Yuzhong of Jeonju fled as well; the Japanese pressed toward Seoul.

sentences.zh: 貴別遣副將解生守稷山，朝鮮亦令都體察使李元翼出忠清道遮賊鋒。

translations.literal: Gui separately dispatched Vice Commander Xie Sheng to guard Jisan; Korea also ordered Inspector-General Yi Won-yuk to exit Chungcheong Circuit to block the enemy spearhead.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui sent Vice Commander Xie Sheng to hold Jisan, while the Koreans ordered Inspector-General Yi Won-yuk to block the Japanese advance through Chungcheong.

sentences.zh: 生頗有斬獲功，參將彭友德亦破賊青山。

translations.literal: Sheng had considerable merit in cutting and capturing; Assistant Commander Peng Youde also broke the enemy at Qingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Sheng won notable kills; Peng Youde defeated the enemy at Qingshan.

sentences.zh: 倭將行長退屯井邑，清正還慶州。

translations.literal: Wo general Yukinaga withdrew to camp at Jeongnyeong; Kiyomasa returned to Gyeongju.
translations.idiomatic: Konishi Yukinaga pulled back to Jeongnyeong, and Kato Kiyomasa to Gyeongju.

sentences.zh: 經略邢玠、經理楊鎬先後至，分兵三協：左李如梅，右李芳春、解生，中高策。

translations.literal: Commissioner Xing Jie and Manager Yang Hao arrived in succession; troops were divided into three columns: left Li Rumei, right Li Fangchun and Xie Sheng, center Gao Ce.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Xing Jie and Manager Yang Hao arrived in turn and divided the army into three wings—Rumei on the left, Fangchun and Xie Sheng on the right, Gao Ce in the center.

sentences.zh: 貴與鎬督左右協兵專攻清正。

translations.literal: Gui with Hao supervised left and right column troops specifically attacking Kiyomasa.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui and Yang Hao directed the left and right wings against Kato Kiyomasa.

sentences.zh: 策駐宜寧，東援兩協，西扼行長。

translations.literal: Ce garrisoned Uiryung, aided east the two columns, west contained Yukinaga.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ce held Uiryung, supporting the eastern wings while blocking Yukinaga to the west.

sentences.zh: 諸軍至慶州，倭悉退屯蔚山，如梅誘敗之。

translations.literal: When the armies reached Gyeongju, the Wo all withdrew to garrison Ulsan; Rumei lured and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The allied armies reached Gyeongju; the Japanese fell back to Ulsan, where Rumei baited and routed them.

sentences.zh: 清正退保島山，築三砦自固。

translations.literal: Kiyomasa retreated to hold Waesan, building three redoubts to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Kiyomasa withdrew to Waesan and fortified three redoubts.

sentences.zh: 遊擊茅國器率死士拔其砦，斬馘六百五十，諸軍遂進圍其城。

translations.literal: Mobile Corps Commander Mao Guoqi led death soldiers to storm their redoubts, cutting six hundred fifty heads; the armies then advanced to besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Guoqi led a suicide squad that stormed a redoubt and took six hundred fifty heads, and the allies moved to besiege the fortress.

sentences.zh: 城新築以石，堅甚，將士仰攻多死。

translations.literal: The city was newly built with stone, very solid; officers and soldiers assaulting upward many died.
translations.idiomatic: The walls were freshly built of stone and extremely strong; many died in the uphill assaults.

sentences.zh: 圍十日，倭襲敗生兵。

translations.literal: Besieging ten days, the Wo raided and defeated Sheng's troops.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days of siege the Japanese counterattacked and routed Xie Sheng's force.

sentences.zh: 明年正月二日，行長來援，九將兵俱潰。

translations.literal: The next year first month second day Yukinaga came to relieve; the nine generals' troops all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the first month, Yukinaga arrived with reinforcements and the allied commanders' armies collapsed.

sentences.zh: 賊張旗幟江上，鎬大懼，倉皇撤師，以捷奏。

translations.literal: The rebels spread banners on the river; Hao was greatly afraid, hastily withdrew troops, and memorialized victory.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese lined the river with banners; Yang Hao panicked, withdrew in disarray, and reported a victory.

sentences.zh: 既而敗狀聞，帝罷鎬，責貴以功贖。

translations.literal: Before long the news of defeat was heard; the emperor dismissed Hao and allowed Gui to redeem guilt with merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the truth came out, the emperor dismissed Yang Hao and let Ma Gui redeem himself through further service.

sentences.zh: 與劉綎、陳璘、董一元分四路。

translations.literal: With Liu Ting, Chen Lin, and Dong Yiyuan they divided into four routes.
translations.idiomatic: He split his forces into four columns with Liu Ting, Chen Lin, and Dong Yiyuan.

sentences.zh: 貴居東，當清正，數戰有功。

translations.literal: Gui held the east, opposing Kiyomasa; in several battles he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui took the eastern wing opposite Kato Kiyomasa and won credit in repeated clashes.

sentences.zh: 會平秀吉死，官軍益力攻。

translations.literal: When news came that Hideyoshi had died, the government army pressed the attack harder.
translations.idiomatic: When word arrived that Hideyoshi was dead, the imperial armies redoubled their assault.

sentences.zh: 十一月，清正先遁，貴遂入島山、西浦，諸路共俘斬二千二百有奇。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Kiyomasa fled first; Gui then entered Waesan and Seopo; all routes together captured and beheaded more than two thousand two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Kato Kiyomasa fled first; Ma Gui then moved into Waesan and Seopo, and the columns together killed or captured more than twenty-two hundred enemy.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，旋師。

translations.literal: The next year in the third month, the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 進右都督，予世廕。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Regional Commander and granted hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Regional Commander and granted hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，命貴鎮遼東。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year Gui was ordered to garrison Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-eight Ma Gui was appointed to command Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 泰寧炒花素桀驁，九子各將兵，他部宰賽、暖兔又助之。

translations.literal: The Taining chieftain Chaohua was by nature fierce and unyielding; his nine sons each commanded troops, and chiefs Zaisai and Nuantu of other tribes also aided him.
translations.idiomatic: Chaohua of the Taining Mongols had long been fierce and unruly; each of his nine sons led his own force, while Zaisai and Nuantu of other tribes lent support.

sentences.zh: 邊將畏戰，但以增歲賞為事，寇益無所忌。

translations.literal: Border generals feared battle and only made increasing annual bounty their business; raiders grew ever more unchecked.
translations.idiomatic: Border commanders feared fighting and contented themselves with buying peace through ever larger annual gifts, so the raiders grew bolder.

sentences.zh: 明年，臨邊要賞，將士出不意擊之，拔營遁，徙額力素居焉。

translations.literal: The next year, when they came to the border demanding bounty, officers and soldiers struck them unawares; they abandoned their camp and fled, and Gui moved Emülüsu to occupy it.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when they came to the border demanding tribute, Ma Gui's troops caught them by surprise; they abandoned camp and fled, and he resettled the site at Emülüsu.

sentences.zh: 其地忽天鳴地震，炒花驚懼，再徙渡老河，去邊幾四百里，其第三子色特哂之，南移可哥毋林，伺隙入犯。
