translations.literal: That place suddenly had heaven-thunder and earthquake; Chaohua was alarmed and afraid, again moved across the Laohu River, nearly four hundred li from the border; his third son Setese moved south to Kewumu Woods, watching for gaps to raid inward.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven thundered and the earth shook there; terrified, Chaohua withdrew again across the Laohu River, nearly four hundred li from the frontier. His third son Setese moved south to Kewumu Woods and waited for a chance to raid.

sentences.zh: 貴伏兵敗之，追北至白雲山，斬馘三百四十有奇。

translations.literal: Gui set an ambush and defeated them, pursuing north to White Cloud Mountain; severed heads numbered more than three hundred forty.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui ambushed and routed them, chasing them as far north as White Cloud Mountain and claiming more than three hundred forty heads.

sentences.zh: 色特憤，謀復仇。

translations.literal: Setese was enraged and plotted revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Setese burned with anger and plotted revenge.

sentences.zh: 糾宰賽、以兒鄧，皆不應。

translations.literal: He rallied Zaisai and Yiriden; neither responded.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to rally Zaisai and Yiriden, but both refused.

sentences.zh: 乃東糾卜言顧、伯要兒，西糾哈剌漢乃蠻，合犯清河，皆潰。

translations.literal: Thereupon he rallied Buyan Gu in the east and Boya'er in the west, and Harhan Naiman; together they invaded Qinghe and all were routed.
translations.idiomatic: He then gathered Buyan Gu and Boya'er in the east and Harhan Naiman in the west, and they jointly struck Qinghe—but all were driven off in defeat.

sentences.zh: 以兒鄧等懼，代炒花求款，邊境乃寧。

translations.literal: Yiriden and the others were afraid; on Chaohua's behalf they sought peace, and the border region then was calm.
translations.idiomatic: Yiriden and his allies, fearing reprisals, sued for peace on Chaohua's behalf, and the frontier quieted.

sentences.zh: 明年，插漢虎墩兔以三萬騎入掠穆家堡。

translations.literal: The next year the Chahar leader Hudun Tu with thirty thousand horsemen entered and plundered Mujia Fort.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Hudun Tu of the Chahars led thirty thousand cavalry to raid Mujia Fort.

sentences.zh: 禦之，敗去。

translations.literal: Gui defended against them; they were defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui met them and drove them off in defeat.

sentences.zh: 其夏，貴引病乞罷，詔乘傳歸。

translations.literal: That summer Gui pleaded illness to request dismissal; an edict ordered him to return by post-horse relay.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Ma Gui cited illness and asked to be relieved; the throne ordered him home by imperial relay.

sentences.zh: 貴果毅驍捷，善用兵，東西並著功伐。

translations.literal: Gui was resolute, brave, and swift; skilled in using troops; east and west alike he achieved military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui was resolute, swift, and skilled in command, winning distinction on both the eastern and western fronts.

sentences.zh: 先後承特賜者七，錫世廕者六。

translations.literal: All told he received special imperial gifts seven times and was granted hereditary privilege six times.
translations.idiomatic: Over his career he received seven special imperial gifts and six grants of hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 及歿，予祭葬。

translations.literal: When he died, sacrificial rites and burial honors were granted.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the court granted him sacrificial and funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 稱一時良將焉。

translations.literal: He may be called a good general of his time.
translations.idiomatic: He was reckoned among the finest generals of his age.

sentences.zh: 兄 錦

translations.literal: Elder brother: Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Ma Jin

sentences.zh: 兄錦，少從父行陣，有戰功。

translations.literal: Elder brother Jin from youth followed his father in the ranks and had battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Ma Jin had campaigned at his father's side from boyhood and won battle honors.

sentences.zh: 累官千總，協守大同右衛。

translations.literal: He accumulated office to chiliarch and jointly guarded Datong Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Rising to the rank of chiliarch, he helped garrison Datong Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 千戶魏昂者，坐罪亡入沙漠，引寇至城下，挾取妻子，錦伏甲擒之。

translations.literal: A chiliarch named Wei Ang, having committed a crime, fled into the desert and led raiders to the city walls, taking hostages of wives and children; Jin hid armored men and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: When the chiliarch Wei Ang fled into the desert after a crime and brought raiders to the walls to seize hostages, Ma Jin concealed armed men and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 俺答圍城，數突圍，城卒完。

translations.literal: Altan besieged the city; Jin several times sallied out; the city in the end remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: When Altan besieged the city, Jin led repeated sorties and kept the walls intact.

sentences.zh: 尋以殺人，並父奪官下吏。

translations.literal: Soon for killing a man, both he and his father were stripped of office and handed to the magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he and his father were stripped of rank and handed to the magistrates for a killing.

sentences.zh: 當事以塞上方用兵，而錦父子兄弟並敢戰，曲法貸之。

translations.literal: Officials, because the border was then at war and Jin with father and brothers together were all daring in battle, bent the law and pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: With the frontier already at war and the Ma Jin family all proven fighters, the authorities bent the law and let them off.

sentences.zh: 屢遷宣府遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Mobile Corps Commander of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly until he became Mobile Corps Commander of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 以勤王功，進秩一等，遷大同參將。

translations.literal: For merit in aiding the throne, his rank advanced one grade and he was transferred to regimental vice commander of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in the campaign to defend the capital, his rank rose one step and he became regimental vice commander at Datong.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，進本鎮副總兵，從趙岢出塞敗寇兵，與弟貴並有保境功。

translations.literal: At the start of Longqing he was advanced to vice regional commander of that garrison; following Zhao Ke beyond the pass he defeated raider troops; with younger brother Gui he together had merit in protecting the border region.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Longqing reign he was made vice regional commander of his own garrison; he followed Zhao Ke beyond the pass to defeat raiders, and he and his brother Ma Gui shared credit for securing the frontier.

sentences.zh: 俺答納款，錦招塞外叛人歸者甚眾。

translations.literal: When Altan accepted peace, Jin recruited many returnees among rebels beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: After Altan made peace, Ma Jin persuaded many deserting tribesmen beyond the passes to come back.

sentences.zh: 萬曆五年，擢山西總兵官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wanli he was promoted to regional commander-in-chief of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year five he was appointed regional commander of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 尋改鎮宣府，卒。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to garrison Xuanfu; he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was shortly after transferred to command Xuanfu, where he died.

sentences.zh: 錦子承勳，遼東副總兵，都督僉事，南京後府僉書。

translations.literal: Jin's son Chengliang: Liaodong vice regional commander, assistant regional commander, secretary in the Nanjing rear bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jin's son Chengliang served as Liaodong vice regional commander, assistant regional commander, and secretary in the Nanjing rear bureau.

sentences.zh: 從子承恩，都督同知，宣府、延綏、大同總兵官。

translations.literal: Nephew Chengen: regional vice commander, regional commander-in-chief of Xuanfu, Yan-sui, and Datong.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Chengen rose to regional vice commander and held regional commands at Xuanfu, Yan-sui, and Datong.

sentences.zh: 更曆諸鎮，以勇力聞。

translations.literal: He passed through the various garrisons in turn and was known for bravery and strength.
translations.idiomatic: He served successive frontier posts and was known for raw courage.

sentences.zh: 後起援遼東，屢退避，下獄當死。

translations.literal: Later recalled to aid Liaodong, he repeatedly withdrew and evaded; imprisoned, he was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Later recalled to reinforce Liaodong, he repeatedly shied from battle; thrown into prison, he was condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 詔納馬八百匹免罪，其家遂破。

translations.literal: An edict allowed him to pay eight hundred horses to be absolved of guilt; his household thereupon was ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The throne let him buy clemency with eight hundred horses, and his family was ruined.

sentences.zh: 承詔，寧夏參將。

translations.literal: Chengzhao: Ningxia regimental vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhao was regimental vice commander of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 從平哱拜有功。

translations.literal: Following the suppression of Pai Bai he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in the campaign to suppress Pai Bai.

sentences.zh: 後為蒼頭所弑。

translations.literal: Later he was murdered by a household slave.
translations.idiomatic: He was later murdered by a household slave.

sentences.zh: 承訓，薊鎮副總兵。

translations.literal: Chengxun: vice regional commander of Ji garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun was vice regional commander of Ji.

sentences.zh: 承宣，洮、岷副總兵。

translations.literal: Chengxuan: vice regional commander of Tao and Min.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxuan was vice regional commander on the Tao–Min frontier.

sentences.zh: 承宗，遼東副總兵。

translations.literal: Chengzong: Liaodong vice regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong was Liaodong vice regional commander.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，戰死沙嶺。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianqi, he died in battle at Shaling.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianqi reign he was killed in action at Shaling.

sentences.zh: 麻氏多將才。

translations.literal: The Ma clan had many general talents.
translations.idiomatic: The Ma family produced many men of military talent.

sentences.zh: 人以方鐵嶺李氏，曰「東李西麻」。

translations.literal: People compared them with the Liaodong Li clan of Tieling, saying "Li in the east, Ma in the west."
translations.idiomatic: People likened them to the Li clan of Tieling in the east and called the pair "Li in the East, Ma in the West."

sentences.zh: 贊曰：自俺答款宣、大，薊門設守固，而遼獨被兵。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Since Altan made peace with Xuan and Da, Ji's gate was guarded firmly, yet Liaodong alone bore the brunt of arms.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: After Altan made peace with Xuanfu and Datong, Ji was strongly garrisoned, yet Liaodong alone bore the brunt of war.

sentences.zh: 成梁遂擅戰功，至剖符受封，震耀一時，倘亦有天幸歟！

translations.literal: Chengliang then monopolized military merit, reaching the splitting of tally and receiving enfeoffment, dazzling his age—might there also have been heaven's favor!
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengliang then monopolized military glory, rising to split tally and receive enfeoffment and dazzle his age—perhaps heaven favored him after all!

sentences.zh: 麻貴宣力東西，勳閥可稱。

translations.literal: Ma Gui exerted himself east and west; as a meritorious house he may be named.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui served with distinction on both fronts—a meritorious house in its own right.

sentences.zh: 兩家子弟，多曆要鎮，是以時論以李、麻並列。

translations.literal: The sons of both clans served many key garrisons; hence contemporaries paired the Li and Ma names.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of both houses held one key garrison after another, so contemporaries ranked the Li and Ma clans together.

sentences.zh: 然列戟擁麾，世傳將種，而恇怯退避，隳其家聲。

translations.literal: Yet arraying halberds and bearing standards, generals by heredity, some cravenly withdrew and evaded, ruining their family renown.
translations.idiomatic: Yet men born to halberds and banners, heirs to a martial line, cravenly held back and ruined their houses' good name.

sentences.zh: 語曰「將門有將」，諸人得無愧乎！

translations.literal: The saying goes, "A general's house produces generals"—can these men be without shame!
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb has it, "A general's house breeds generals"—should these men not feel ashamed!
